title: Hannah and Tatiana: A Unique Duo
excerpt: When I started getting into the third book of the series, titled Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, I knew I wanted to include Tatiana in my story. When Hannah met her, she was at a point in her life…
html:
When I started getting into the third book of the series, titled Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, I knew I wanted to include Tatiana in my story. When Hannah met her, she was at a point in her life where she felt like she couldn’t do anything right. But meeting Tatiana marked a turning point for Hannah. Their conversation on the plane as they headed back to Paris made me reflect on my own life and reminded me that life is short. When you feel others trying to bring you down, hold on to a memory that made you feel proud — revisit that moment and you’ll find yourself feeling stronger.

As Tatiana is a witness to what goes down near the end of Paris Noir, I knew I wanted to include her in my fourth book as well. Her life has shifted in many ways by the time we reach this next installment; she has become someone who goes out and does what she does best—changing people’s lives in the most unexpected, quietly profound ways. Much like she is to me in real life, in Hannah’s life Tatiana is the light that appears when everything feels dark and uncertain. When we last left Tatiana, Hannah had just asked her to become Shayla’s godmother, a role that promises to deepen their bond and send both of their lives in new, surprising directions.

At the start of the fourth book, Smith asks Hannah where Tatiana is. Hannah explains that Tatiana has stayed behind in Miami to care for Shayla while Hannah pursues leads and tries to solve Laura’s murder. As the story unfolds, readers will notice just how much Hannah’s relationship with Tatiana has deepened and how much Tatiana’s steady presence has helped her grow. While Hannah and Rafael, accompanied by Stu, travel to Lucerne to seek the antidote at Die Klinik den Geist Zu halen, Tatiana remains devoted to watching over Shayla, tending to her needs and doing everything she can to keep her safe.

As the story progresses, Tatiana does something especially thoughtful and chooses to surprise Hannah, bringing Shayla along so she can be close to her. That simple act of kindness confirms to Hannah that she made the right choice in naming Tatiana her daughter’s godmother. After Shayla is kidnapped, Hannah is understandably furious with Tatiana, but once Shayla is safely rescued, Hannah’s anger toward Tatiana gradually subsides. As the narrative draws toward its conclusion, Tatiana becomes more involved when Rafael ends up in the hospital; she remains by his side, while Hannah departs for Giethoorn to pursue the answers she needs to unravel the murders and to search for the antidote.

When they all return to the states, Tatiana explains to Hannah her dilemma. Writing Tatiana’s dilemma was perhaps one of my favorite parts to craft, because it highlights just how much she has grown. Once an illusionist, she has become someone people can genuinely look up to. Hearing her predicament brings Hannah closer to cracking the case, and in the end Tatiana is the one who must take responsibility for saving Rafael and everyone else, especially because of skills she learned in her former life. In the fifth installment of the Hannah Walker Mystery Series titled Shadows of the Past A Deadly Riddle, she will have an even bigger role in which she will turn into the hero, along with Hannah and Rafael
seo_title: Hannah and Tatiana: A Unique Duo

title: Rafael, a hero in Hannah’s life inspired by R.G.
excerpt: When I first began writing the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, I knew I wanted to explore the deep, protective love a godfather feels for his goddaughter. Rafael’s character was inspired by a former…
html:
When I first began writing the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, I knew I wanted to explore the deep, protective love a godfather feels for his goddaughter. Rafael’s character was inspired by a former administrator of justice, Professor R.G., whose quiet strength and guidance shaped me. Only a few people know who he truly is and how profoundly his influence and example impacted my life.

When we first meet Hannah, she feels profoundly lonely, a sense sharpened by Rafael’s sudden return to her life. The long years he spent serving as a law enforcement officer kept them apart, creating a distance that time never quite healed. Hannah had never fully understood the depth of her godfather’s love for her until he began hiring bodyguards and even made moves to place her in witness protection.

One thing about Hannah in the series is how much her relationship with her godfather has evolved over time. Their bond is severely tested when Hannah is accused of a crime and thrown in jail, and it is in that dark moment she finally sees just how deeply Rafael loves and protects her. After the dramatic reveal in the first book, Hannah boldly asks Rafael to take her on a European adventure — a request he willingly agrees to fulfill because his love for her outweighs any hesitation.

When they moved to Paris for three years, Rafael knew that Hannah was not doing well; nonetheless he was there for her at every step of the way. Perhaps the most painful part of all came when Hannah lost her memory and, in a moment of confusion and fear, yelled at him that she hated him — words that shattered Rafael to the very core. Writing the letter to Hannah during the drafting process is what finally broke me; I still cry when I look back at the manuscript.

Few people truly understand how and why I decided to have Hannah lose her memory. In Paris Noir, Hannah becomes increasingly worried about Rafael’s safety. She senses that an arch‑nemesis must alter the hero’s life in a profound way. She also mentions to Rafael that he cannot keep pulling her from the path of oncoming trains. I wanted to go all out with Paris Noir. Rafael has always been somewhat enigmatic—he’s the kind of man who knows people who know other people. He has contacts who can arrange witness protection, he speaks multiple languages, and he moves in shadowed networks. From the start I knew the story needed to center on him and on how his relationship with Hannah is irrevocably changed. After the events of Paris Noir, we move on to the Thirteenth Riddle A Poisoned Silence. The relationship has been shattered and Hannah hates him, until he gets poisoned. This is when the script is flipped. Instead of Rafael protecting Hannah, it is Hannah who is going to make sure that she protects Rafael at all costs.

In the fifth book, titled Shadows of the Past: A Deadly Riddle, Rafael’s role will expand even further, and he will stand by his goddaughter when she discovers who she truly is, where she comes from, and the painful truth that her father never loved her. That revelation only draws them closer, pushing Rafael into full protective godfather mode. It is in these moments of danger and vulnerability that Hannah finally understands how profoundly Rafael has been her true hero.
seo_title: Rafael, a hero in Hannah’s life inspired by R.G.

title: Tatiana’s role in Shadows of the Past: A Deadly Riddle takes her from being attacked to becoming the hero.
excerpt: Tatiana… the former illusionist whom Hannah met in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, now returns with a larger, more pivotal role in the upcoming fifth installment of the Hannah Walker Mystery Series. As…
html:
Tatiana… the former illusionist whom Hannah met in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, now returns with a larger, more pivotal role in the upcoming fifth installment of the Hannah Walker Mystery Series. As Shayla’s godmother, Tatiana is the steady, level-headed presence who keeps her composure and takes charge whenever things begin to take a dark turn. With The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence, Tatiana’s role shifted from a quietly supportive guardian into a more assertive, strategic force — the kind of figure who not only steadies the frightened but also probes the shadows, making calculated moves to protect those she loves. Writing Tatiana’s Dilemma was perhaps one of my favorite moments to craft in TTRAPS, largely because of how dramatically she evolved and how she became the decisive hand that helped Hannah rescue Rafael when he was endangered.

Tatiana has taught Hannah how to be more confident and how to confront the shadows that haunt her. With Rafael, she feels protected and safe, but when it comes to Tatiana, Hannah will always have a soft spot—perhaps because they somehow find a way to truly connect. Through the recurring premonition dreams that continue to plague her, Tatiana will push Hannah to face the demons of both past and present, transforming Hannah’s fears into a renewed and steadier strength.

Will Tatiana find love? Maybe. In the Hannah Walker Mystery Series I want to ensure that not everyone gets a neat, tied-up happy ending; perhaps Tatiana will be the exception, and perhaps she will marry in the next book. One thing is certain… Hannah will be the one to set her up.

How has she evolved from PN to this new fifth series? She’s grown more complex: not only is she fiercely protective of Shayla, but she’s also carefully guarding Hannah’s well‑being and future. Not only will she face direct attacks, but she’ll be thrown into the heart of the action and share responsibility with Rafael as they learn to bring down the antagonist together. As with any superhero tale, an arch‑nemesis emerges. Echoing the third installment, only one character will suffer a devastating, potentially irreparable loss. Will it be Tatiana? Rafael again? Or Hannah? The answers lie in Shadows of the Past: A Deadly Riddle.
seo_title: Tatiana’s Role in Shadows of the Past

title: Deadly College Murders Wins at IIBA!
excerpt: I am thrilled to announce that my first novel, Deadly College Murders, which took me five years to write, has won at the International Impact Book Awards. Winning another award surpasses my…
html:
I am thrilled to announce that my first novel, Deadly College Murders, which took me five years to write, has won at the International Impact Book Awards. Winning another award surpasses my expectations and stands as the brightest highlight of my career as an author. When I opened the email, my hands were shaking and my stomach dropped with a sudden surge of disbelief and joy. Several people had advised me against submitting my manuscript, but I sent it in anyway, and that decision has made all the difference. To receive yet another message from IIBA congratulating me on winning feels nothing short of amazing. Looking back, I remember how many of my professors tried to diminish my dreams of becoming a writer; still, I never gave up. I chose this path, and I am delighted to share that I am now writing the fifth book in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, titled Shadows of the Past: Deadly Riddle. In addition, I have learned that I was awarded a Distinguished Author Award for both Deadly College Murders and The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence, an honor that truly validates every late night and hard-fought draft.

Having secured two more consecutive IIBA awards, I am now recognized as an author who exceeds expectations. I want the world to know who Bree Wilson is, and steadily—step by determined step—I am making a name for myself. Next stop: Hollywood.
seo_title: Deadly College Murders Wins at IIBA!

title: Hannah’s dreams and eerie ghostly visions
excerpt: A recurring theme in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series is Hannah’s dreams. From the very first book she is plagued by relentless premonition dreams that feel unnervingly real; when she wakes she is…
html:
A recurring theme in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series is Hannah’s dreams. From the very first book she is plagued by relentless premonition dreams that feel unnervingly real; when she wakes she is often terrified, her heart pounding and her breath coming fast. How and why does Hannah see these eerie, ghostlike figures? The explanation traces back to the time she developed an obsession with solving a murder and emulating Sherlock Holmes—an obsession that opened a door to visions and possibilities she could never have anticipated. These haunting images can be the spirits of those who died at the college, strangers she has never met, or, on the most troubling nights, the inscrutable hooded figure who keeps returning, silent and watching. At times Hannah is alone in her room, with Rafael next door. Suddenly she hears someone come in and it is the hooded figure. Then, a victim from the college murders sits by her bedside. Hannah questions why they are there, and they tell Hannah…

“Your problem was always being where you shouldn’t be. Listening to the wrong people. On the contrary, had you devoted yourself to writing, you would have saved yourself a lifetime of pain. There were times, in which I thought you were going to be able to be happy. But instead, you buried the last piece of happiness you ever had. And the worst part of all? You were never able to be faithful to anything or anyone. Not even yourself.”

What do the dreams mean? Essentially, they hinge on the idea that if Hannah had committed herself fully to study and writing, none of this would have occurred. They also comment on the double standards woven through the series—an aspect only readers of my books will truly grasp. These dreams will continue in the 5th and 6th book respectively.
seo_title: Hannah’s dreams and eerie ghostly visions

Receiving another award is an incredible honor and stands as a true highlight of my career as an author. The Thirteenth Riddle was perhaps one of the most difficult manuscripts I have ever written, especially because I wanted it to be perfect — to deliver all the dark twists, turns, and riddles exactly as they were imagined. Perhaps one of the most difficult chapters to write was Hannah’s monologue on Grievance. Everything that I was feeling as a person — the quiet resentments, the sudden wells of sadness, the small, sharp regrets — I knew I wanted to weave into Hannah’s world, to let those private currents shape her voice and steer the scene, until the emotion felt both personal and universal. Winning another award is beyond my wildest dreams and a deeply humbling affirmation of the work. Going to these awards is such a wonderful way to meet and get to know other authors, to share stories and form lasting bonds. If you are an author, consider submitting your book to the IIBA today.

title: Proudly Accepting My Second IIBA Award for Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes
excerpt: When I learned Deadly Vows had won, there were no words to describe how happy and emotional I was when I got that email. After years of doubt and discouragement — even from a number of my college…
html:
When I learned Deadly Vows had won, there were no words to describe how happy and emotional I was when I got that email. After years of doubt and discouragement — even from a number of my college professors who insisted I should give up on my writing — there was one voice that had never wavered: RG. I knew that I was going to go to AZ to accept my award, because the first time I had it mailed to me I had wanted the vivid, tangible feeling of holding the trophy in my hands. When I stepped up onto that stage, I felt profoundly empowered, quietly confident, and happier than I had ever been in my life. Getting ready for this, I found myself thinking about a lot of different things; I wondered, “Would I climb up on that stage and break down the way I did in February? Or would I manage to stay composed and not cry?” In the end, this time I did not cry, and the calm pride I felt lingered long after the applause died down. Working on my speech, I knew I was going to thank two very important people: Tatiana, for her relentless support and her bright, shining light, and R.G., for becoming the unexpected inspiration behind the character of Rafael. Getting to go up on stage and be surrounded by such talented people was nothing short of amazing, and I left that evening both grateful and energized — I look forward to more IIBA events and the opportunities they bring.

The event began in the morning with the conference and the opportunity to hear Nim Stant’s tell her story about coming to the United States from Thailand. She carried a dream of becoming a writer and went on to found the International Impact Book Awards. Being recognized for my writing and hard work by IIBA is nothing short of amazing and stands as the highlight of my career as a two-time award-winning author. Next stop… Hollywood.

What I said in my speech:

“Wow, my second international impact book award. First off, I want to thank Nim Stant and the entire IIBA judging panel for selecting my book as a winner. Winning this award is nothing short of amazing and stands as one of the brightest highlights of my career as an award‑winning author. When I learned I had won, I thought back to how many of my college professors tried to diminish my dreams of becoming a writer—except for one who believed in me and kept me going. Their faith, along with the support of readers, family, and colleagues, has sustained me through the long nights of revision and the inevitable doubts, making this recognition all the more meaningful.”
seo_title: Accepting My Second IIBA Award for Deadly Vows

title: Tatiana’s Dilemma and why it was my favorite chapter to write
excerpt: The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence. The continuation of Hannah and Co. The bond between Hannah and Rafael has soured, fraying under the weight of unspoken accusations. Guilt gnaws at Hannah…
html:
The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence. The continuation of Hannah and Co. The bond between Hannah and Rafael has soured, fraying under the weight of unspoken accusations. Guilt gnaws at Hannah constantly. After repeated, unsuccessful attempts to shield Rafael from danger, she finds solace in just two anchors: her steadfast friend Tatiana and her young daughter, Shayla.

Introduced in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, Tatiana first appears to readers as an illusionist who worked alongside Criss Angel. Near the end of that book, Hannah adopts Tatiana’s outlook on life, and—though she barely knows her—Hannah impulsively invites Tatiana to her wedding with Jonathan. It is Tatiana who serves as a crucial witness during the climactic confrontation between Hannah and the culprit. In this new book Tatiana has changed: she has retired from performing illusions and now concentrates on the quieter journey of life, watching over Hannah and offering guidance when needed. She also devotes much of her time to caring for her goddaughter, Shayla.

Perhaps one of my favorite chapters to write is titled “Tatiana’s Dilemma.” Writing that chapter felt essential; it appears near the end of the book, just before the climax, and it highlights how far Tatiana has come. The chapter showcases not only her growth but also how remarkably skilled she is at unraveling mysteries. It is Tatiana who later supplies the crucial idea to Hannah and the others when they return from Giethoorn to the States, explaining to the team that they have been approaching the puzzle from the wrong angle.

She will also be the one responsible for saving Rafael near the end. Her expertise as a former illusionist and quick-thinking sleight of hand will prove crucial in pulling him back from the brink. But will she survive the ordeal? Or will she be silenced by the same poison? The answer lies in The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence.

Check out the excerpt from Tatiana’s Dilemma

“We are looking at this entirely wrong,” Tatiana said, her sharp eyes scanning the exhausted faces of Hannah, Rafael and Smith. “We are treating the antidote and the thirteenth riddle as two separate problems. But your enemy is a sadist, not an anarchist. They wouldn’t design a flawless countdown without a grand finale.”

“Exactly, because it was a distraction to burn our time,” Tatiana countered, leaning against the edge of the map table. “Think about the structure of the game. If the thirteenth riddle demands a confession, then the riddle isn’t just a threat- it’s the transaction. The antidote IS the prize for solving it.”
seo_title: Tatiana’s Dilemma and why it was my favorite chapter to write

title: Deadly Vows wasn’t originally going to be called Deadly Vows.
excerpt: When I decided that DCM would evolve into a series, I began writing the sequel immediately at the close of Deadly College Murders, eagerly plotting the next twists and characters. While still writing…
html:
When I decided that DCM would evolve into a series, I began writing the sequel immediately at the close of Deadly College Murders, eagerly plotting the next twists and characters.

While still writing Deadly College Murders within that five-year span, the sequel’s title wasn’t always fixed as Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes (IIBA Winner April 2026); at first it had been planned as “Wedding and a Murder: Sequel to Deadly College Murders.”

I realized that the title was too long and originally, the story was going to begin where it had originally ended: New York. So how did I come up with the title of the second book? It all boiled down to the wedding between Connie and her fiancée. I needed a believable reason for Hannah to go back to that godforsaken town she had sworn she would never set foot in again. I knew that if I wanted the continuation of the first book, I would need to focus on the murder of Connie and all the tangled secrets that had shadowed her life.

When Hannah speaks with Connie shortly before the tragedy, she senses that Connie is holding back and concealing something important, but she chooses to dismiss the unease and carry on. Mere moments before Hannah would reach the altar, Connie is suddenly murdered, her life taken before she can utter the words “I do.”

After her murder, Hannah tells Rafael that she suspects whoever killed Connie had to be someone tied to her past in college—the same college she attended and later returned to as a professor. The echoes of Connie’s life on that campus, the secrets she kept, and the investigation she was pursuing into King X all point to connections rooted in those earlier years.

Once I had that written, it was how I arrived at the title Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes.

But it wasn’t going to be about Connie’s murder either; this time it would revolve around Hannah’s sudden memory loss and the consuming obsession to uncover who Sofia really was. When Hannah is later cornered by the culprit and savagely beaten into a coma, the unraveling becomes even more urgent; it will fall to Rafael to dig through lies and danger to discover who King X truly is and, ultimately, to piece together the real identity and hidden past of Connie.

As with the first book, the reader MUST pay close attention to each and every one of the suspicious characters, for each of them conceals a fragment that will unlock Hannah’s memory.
seo_title: Deadly Vows wasn’t originally going to be called Deadly Vows.

title: Doug… a disgraced and corrupt cop and a hidden main villain?
excerpt: Doug was first introduced in Deadly College Murders. When Hannah describes him, she explains that Doug had just been fired from the Miami-Dade PD. When he reappears in her life, Doug confides to…
html:
Doug was first introduced in Deadly College Murders. When Hannah describes him, she explains that Doug had just been fired from the Miami-Dade PD. When he reappears in her life, Doug confides to Hannah that he still cannot get past the death of his wife, and that the loss continues to shadow his days and choices.

While he did not have many direct interactions with any of the characters apart from Hannah, he vanished under mysterious circumstances once Hannah was put on trial. In the end, after Hannah confronts the culprit, it is strongly suggested—during a quiet, tense scene in Paris with her godfather—that there may still be one or possibly two principal hidden main masterminds at large, their identities and motives left deliberately unresolved.

Doug resurfaces in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. After Hannah is involved in the accident—caused when a hooded figure forces one of the victims to cut her brakes—she begins dreaming of Doug while she’s in surgery and grows increasingly unsettled, haunted by nagging questions about who he really is and what he truly wants. When Rafael is hospitalized from stress, Hannah confides in her beloved godfather, telling him she plans to travel to Miami to dig deeper and finally uncover the truth about Doug’s identity. Not wanting his goddaughter to go alone, Raf accompanies Hannah to the Miami-Dade station to investigate and peel back layers of Doug’s past. When they learn that he was a disgraced, corrupt cop, Rafael is both shocked and disgusted, prompting a tense exchange with Hannah. He tells her that Doug reminds him of someone he once knew—(Donovan)—and admits he’s frightened for her safety now that she knows who Doug really is and what he might be capable of.

Tragically, as Hannah uncovers the secrets of Sofia’s past, she finds herself in grave danger and is violently attacked — leaving the haunting question: did Doug assault Hannah in New Orleans and cause her to lose her memory? The answers lie in DVEOCC.
seo_title: Doug… a disgraced and corrupt cop and a hidden main villain?

title: Hannah’s struggle with memory loss and Rafael’s pain
excerpt: When I began writing the second book, I knew it had to surpass the first — to be sharper, darker, and more affecting. I asked myself what fresh cruelties I could visit upon Hannah and Rafael to…
html:
When I began writing the second book, I knew it had to surpass the first — to be sharper, darker, and more affecting. I asked myself what fresh cruelties I could visit upon Hannah and Rafael to deepen their trials and test their bond. After the first book’s events, Hannah begged Rafael to take her to Paris, and from that plea their European odyssey began. For three years Rafael was Hannah’s anchor, steadfast beside her through the long nights when nightmares of those who murdered the faculty staff haunted her sleep. Whenever those visions returned, Rafael refused to leave her; he would soothe her with long, aimless walks along the Seine and nights spent watching the Eiffel Tower sparkle at midnight. Their bond felt unbreakable — and I resolved I would be the one to put that to the severest test.

When Daniel calls Hannah to tell her that Connie is getting married, a familiar fear begins to creep back into Hannah’s thoughts about returning to the States. Yet after their conversation, her visions come rushing back; shaken but resolute, she wakes Rafael and tells him she is ready to travel back for Connie’s wedding. After she is murdered, shortly before her wedding, Hannah suspects that someone from her past has come back to haunt her. The issue that haunts Hannah across all three books is that, in trying to protect Rafael and make sure nothing happens to him, she acts in secret and makes choices that ultimately land her in danger. The most daunting scene for me to write is the one in their apartment, when she studies a photo of her and Rafael, murmurs “I’m sorry, Raf, I’m doing this for both of us,” and sets off for New Orleans. She has no idea that it will be the last time she sees her beloved godfather; after confronting the culprit in her hotel, she loses her memory and everything changes.

When Rafael learns that she is in the hospital, he immediately flies to Los Angeles, arriving with worry deeply etched on his face; when she finally awakens, he is shattered to hear the words no godfather wants to hear as Hannah looks up and asks, “Who are you?” — leaving Rafael utterly heartbroken and reeling from the sudden absence of the bond he had trusted and relied on for so long. The pain Rafael carries after the doctor tells him of Hannah’s memory loss is unbearably raw and utterly heartbreaking. Even though she doesn’t remember who he is, at nights Rafael curls up and cries himself to sleep, the tears a quiet confession of his grief. Just seeing Hannah so completely lost, failing to recognize familiar faces and strangers alike, is steadily destroying his very soul. Even though Bree tries to reassure Rafael that everything will eventually be okay, those words do little to ease the persistent ache he still feels.

Hannah felt a lot of pressure from everyone who kept reminding her who she had been in the past. The weight of their expectations tugged at her until she could hardly breathe. The biggest blowout comes near the climax, when she finally explodes at Rafael and tells him off. She yells at him and blames him for all the dangers they have faced together, unleashing months of fear and resentment in a single, raw moment. Then, with a voice edged in pain, she shouts, “I AM NOT THE PERSON YOU WANT ME TO BE! I AM NOT YOUR GODDAUGHTER, I AM NOT HER!” Those brutal words hang in the air; Rafael, shattered, walks away. Not long after, he writes her a heartbreaking letter, one that confirms the distance her outburst has carved between them. It is thanks to this letter that Hannah recovers her memory.

But why have Hannah lose her memory? Hannah had been struggling a great deal over the past three years. Those years were brutal for her, and in the early months Raf would sometimes see her suffer flashbacks, ordinary faces warping into the faces of her tormentors. She once confessed to him that she wished, more than anything, she could forget the things she had been through. It is no wonder my second book won at IIBA!
seo_title: Hannah’s struggle with memory loss and Rafael’s pain

title: Original ending for Deadly College Murders
excerpt: Deadly College Murders… the story of Hannah Walker, a college student who dreams of solving crimes and aspires to be like Sherlock Holmes. It took me five long years to write this novel, during which…
html:
Deadly College Murders… the story of Hannah Walker, a college student who dreams of solving crimes and aspires to be like Sherlock Holmes. It took me five long years to write this novel, during which I had to learn and refine my craft to perfect it in every possible way. The narrative went through numerous different conclusions, and I kept wrestling with the ending until it finally fell into place. Hannah was never meant to finish her journey in Paris; the original plan had her heading off to New York with Daniel. Rafael’s fate also shifted: rather than taking his goddaughter to Europe with him, he chose to remain behind after she asked for time to decide what she truly wanted, especially following her tense confrontation with the culprit near the story’s climax.

At first, I planned for the story to end with Hannah and Daniel in New York, but my 2023 trip to Europe inspired me to change the narrative, placing Hannah in Europe with Rafael instead. I wanted to focus more on the bond between Rafael and Hannah, which deepened when Hannah was in jail and Rafael was the only one there for her. Despite his duties as a college professor, he stood by her side, especially during the heartbreak of her miscarriage.Near the end of the story, after confronting the culprit, Rafael has a heartfelt talk with Hannah, telling her that only she can decide what she truly wants in life. Does she really want to be with Daniel, or would she rather focus on continuing to love herself more? This leads Hannah to say “No” to Daniel. While she appreciated his desire to be with her, she couldn’t get past the fact that he had lied and rejected her when he was actually in love with her. Hannah realized she didn’t need to be with him to be happy—she was already content as she was, with her godfather by her side.

Instead of ending up in New York City, Hannah told Rafael she wanted to go to Paris, right after returning from the Cayman Islands. She realized she needed a change of scenery, and the story wraps up in Paris with Rafael by her side, helping her recover over the next three years—physically, psychologically, and emotionally. Some have asked me “If you could do it all again, would you change the ending?” No, I would not change the ending
seo_title: Original ending for Deadly College Murders

title: Frigon… a villain to the very end
excerpt: Detective Frigon. Her mission had been clear from the very beginning: to see that Hannah Walker was held accountable for the college crimes she appeared to be framed for. She pursued the case with…
html:
Detective Frigon. Her mission had been clear from the very beginning: to see that Hannah Walker was held accountable for the college crimes she appeared to be framed for. She pursued the case with steady purpose, determined that justice be done—contrasting sharply with Smith, who, as the books unfolded, grew into an unexpected ally for Hannah.

When we first met Frigon in Deadly College Murders, she had been partners with Smith for the longest time, and she was the one who steadily put the idea into Smith’s head that Hannah was responsible for the college murders. When Hannah is arrested, Frigon relentlessly blames her at every turn, pushing accusations and public suspicion so far that it culminates in Hannah lashing out and attacking her.

Even after Hannah was released from jail, and even after enduring the heartbreak of her miscarriage, Frigon still insisted she was guilty and could not fathom why the authorities had let her go and allowed her to walk free. After Hannah finally learns who the true culprit is, she chooses not to call Frigon; instead she phones Smith, because she trusts him, and because although Smith had been antagonistic toward her at first, he had shown her moments of kindness. When Frigon learned that Smith had offered Hannah a position, she reacted with a mixture of surprise and resentment, unable to hide how threatened he felt by the turn of events. Although she thanked Smith for the offer, Hannah informed him, she wanted to go to Europe to clear her head and start fresh.

The next time we encounter Frigon is in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. When Hannah returns to the States to investigate Connie’s murders, Frigon remains cold and antagonistic toward her, viewing Hannah’s presence as an unwelcome disruption to the established course of the investigation. The only moment Frigon’s hard exterior cracks is when she is about to tell Hannah that she knows who murdered Connie; tragically, before she can speak, the culprit silences her permanently to ensure the truth never comes out.

Frigon is based on someone I met a while ago. She is also loosely modeled after the sheriffs from the Aurora Teagarden Mysteries and Murder, She Baked.
seo_title: Frigon… a villain to the very end

title: The hero and the arch-nemesis — the one who turns the hero’s life upside down.
excerpt: An arch nemesis… When I began the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, I knew I wanted a true Arch Nemesis—someone to haunt and challenge not just Hannah but also the people closest to her, whether that be…
html:
An arch nemesis… When I began the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, I knew I wanted a true Arch Nemesis—someone to haunt and challenge not just Hannah but also the people closest to her, whether that be Jonathan or even Rafael. An arch nemesis must do more than obstruct; they have to alter the hero’s path and force hard choices. In Hannah’s story, her hero is her godfather Rafael, a man shaped by a heavy, shadowed past that continues to ripple through their lives.

Rafael loves Hannah more than anything, and the choices he made in the past have come back to haunt him. In Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes, following the events of the first book, Hannah remains the central figure and continues to bear the brunt of their shared tragedy. Struggling with memory loss and the slow, painful process of piecing together who she once was, Hannah begins to see Rafael as responsible for much of the suffering they endure.

And that is how I knew what Paris Noir was going to be about. The shadows of Rafael’s past, and the consequences of the choices he made, are what will shape the outcome of the series. As mentioned at the start, an arch-nemesis must alter the hero’s life; in Paris Noir, that hero is Rafael, and it is Donovan’s actions that change the course of events for Paris Noir — a conflict whose repercussions will carry forward into The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence.

Donovan is a ruthless, cold, and calculating figure whose deep-seated hatred for Rafael fuels an obsessive drive for revenge. He is painfully aware that Rafael’s greatest weakness is Hannah, and he deliberately exploits that vulnerability, believing that by inflicting pain on her he can wound Rafael where it hurts most.

Which is precisely why what Donovan does ultimately alters Rafael’s life for the worse, leaving him to shoulder a crushing guilt he will carry for the rest of his days. Who survives in this third installment of the series? The answers wait in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession.
seo_title: The Hero and the Arch-Nemesis

title: Hannah’s showdown with the culprit showcases a unique approach, setting her apart from Hallmark’s typical leading mystery ladies in the way she unravels the truth.
excerpt: Aurora “Roe” Teagarden, Hannah Swensen from Murder She Baked, Tess Harper from Crossword Mysteries, Hailey Dean from Hailey Dean Mysteries… what do all these women have in common? In every episode…
html:
Aurora “Roe” Teagarden, Hannah Swensen from Murder She Baked, Tess Harper from Crossword Mysteries, Hailey Dean from Hailey Dean Mysteries… what do all these women have in common? In every episode I’ve seen on Hallmark Movies and Mysteries, one thing stands out: these women simply cannot hide their reactions when they discover the culprit. They make it unmistakably clear to the killer that they know who did it. For instance, in the first Hailey Dean movie — where Hailey, a former prosecutor turned therapist, unravels the case — the moment she identifies the murderer she reacts so plainly and immediately that there’s no mistaking her certainty.

When Hannah uncovers who murdered Ron in Murder She Baked A Chocolate Chip Cookie Mystery, the killer realizes Hannah has unmasked them. When Roe discovers Sabrina is behind the killings in A Game of Cat and Mouse: An Aurora Teagarden Mystery, Bri immediately recognizes that Roe has identified her as the murderer. I knew I needed to ensure Hannah stood out from these other leading ladies.

When we first met Hannah in Deadly College Murders, we quickly learned she aspired to be like Sherlock Holmes — eager to unravel a good mystery. After serving time in jail for the murder of Professor Gonzalez, she is now more determined than ever to unmask the real killer and prove who set her up. A recurring theme throughout the books is the premonition-like dreams that haunt her nights, and how nearly every person she has crossed paths with insists that, had she continued to devote herself to painting, she would have avoided all of this turmoil. What sets Hannah apart from the usual Hallmark leading ladies is simple: she moves with calculated caution. Hannah takes deliberate steps to keep the hooded figure from discovering that she is investigating, and she knows clever ways to distract and mislead that shadowy threat.

With Roe and the other Hallmark leading ladies, they make it obvious to the killer: their eyes widen, they fumble for an excuse — the tired cliche, “I left the cookies in my oven.” Hannah Walker, by contrast, flips the script and becomes the blackbird. She deliberately feeds the killer false information to draw them out, choosing to be strategic and intentionally dangerous rather than naïvely exposed. By keeping her cards close to her chest and setting calculated traps, she outsmarts the culprit. That’s also why she constantly reminds Rafael that new dangers are coming every day, never letting them forget the threats that lurk around the corner.
seo_title: Hannah’s Showdown: Unlike Any Hallmark Mystery Heroine

Christina

Daughter of Laura Gonzalez. Stepdaughter of Gonzalez, the man who hated Hannah with a passion. Christina is your typical college student — young, determined, and sweet, utterly devoted to her mother Laura. She has always struggled with her stepfather, a man who despised her simply because she was not his biological daughter.

She never got to know her real father, Stu, a doctor who will become the crucial figure in locating the antidote that can save Rafael. Like Laura, Hannah will discover that Christina harbored her own hidden truths, and that the treatment Christina received in Lucerne is connected to the mysterious events that befell Hannah in Paris.

title: Character Profile: Det. Smith… From Villain to Ally
excerpt: Detective Smith His determined nature and near-obsessive drive to ensure Hannah Walker paid for her perceived transgressions in Deadly College Murders initially defined Smith as the story’s…
html:
Detective Smith

His determined nature and near-obsessive drive to ensure Hannah Walker paid for her perceived transgressions in Deadly College Murders initially defined Smith as the story’s antagonist. Over time, however, his rigid vendetta softened, and he transformed from a one-dimensional villain into a reluctant ally, ultimately collaborating with Hannah.

When Hannah uncovered who was behind the murders, Smith surprised her by offering her a position to work alongside him in the police department. Hannah, however, gently declined his offer, explaining that she did not feel ready to take on the responsibilities of a detective.

When Hannah returns to town in Deadly Vows, Smith asks her to stay out of the investigation, worried she might be killed again as she nearly was the first time. When Hannah later loses her memory, Smith steps up to help Rafael and the team determine who is responsible for the new string of killings. Though he nearly loses his life in the process, Smith ultimately perseveres and is the one who makes the arrest after Hannah regains her memory.

In Paris Noir Deadly Obsession, Smith is the one who will be in charge of defending Hannah against Mason and Donovan, who are determined to make her life a living hell and attempt to frame her for the recent string of killings.

He is also the one who will arrest Hannah once again, this time at Hannah’s request, since she wants to uncover who Bree really is. Although he initially objects to the plan, once Rafael gives his approval Smith arranges for Hannah to have protection while in jail and tells her she has two weeks to uncover the truth. Smith is also the officer who will be present at the wedding and ultimately the one to unmask and bring down the culprit. Near the end of Paris Noir, Smith calls Hannah to tell her he found Laura’s body, along with a letter and a riddle addressed to her.

In the Thirteenth Riddle, A Poisoned Silence, Smith and Hannah work together, now officially partnered, navigating tense investigations side by side. He becomes the one she turns to for guidance when she most needs it, offering steady advice and reassurance. He explains that Rafael's actions stem from a desire to protect her, rooted in his deepest fear of losing her.

Initially he was going to be the antagonist, but as time went by and as I started to develop his character, I decided to turn him into an ally of the Walker-Smith clan. He had been simply trying to do his job, and at first the evidence against Hannah seemed overwhelming. However, after she was thrown in jail and sentenced to death, Smith came to realize that Hannah was innocent. He even went so far as to offer her a job working with him, an offer she declined. I wanted Smith to become an ally because, through everything he witnessed, he recognized that Hannah was fundamentally a good person.

Perhaps my favorite scene to write was in Paris Noir, when Hannah pleads with him to arrest her. He tells her he doesn't want to, until she cheekily reminds him how much fun it was the last time he slipped her into handcuffs… and suddenly his resistance softens. Smith will have even more character development in Shadows of her Past, A Hannah Walker Mystery.
seo_title: Character Profile: Det. Smith… From Villain to Ally

title: Character Profile: Laura
excerpt: Laura Gonzalez Ex Wife of Professor Gonzalez. The man who was murdered at the beginning of Deadly College Murders, and the woman whose testimony helped seal Hannah’s fate at her trial. Laura is a…
html:
Laura Gonzalez

Ex Wife of Professor Gonzalez. The man who was murdered at the beginning of Deadly College Murders, and the woman whose testimony helped seal Hannah’s fate at her trial. Laura is a woman haunted by the consequences of choices she made long ago. Once a simple, determined person, she set out to destroy Hannah in retaliation for what she believed Hannah had done to her husband. Yet behind closed doors the truth was more complicated: Laura had been deeply unhappy in her marriage to Gonzalez and carried knowledge of many of his secrets—secrets she deliberately kept to herself. In a late turn of conscience she writes a letter to Hannah, offering an apology for the role she played in her downfall, though Hannah never receives it while Laura is alive, as Laura herself is killed at the start of the fourth book, The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence.

The only good thing that Laura had was the fierce devotion she felt for her daughter Christina, who returned that love with equal intensity. What Laura does not know is that someone is stalking them both, and a deadly threat is closing in. It will fall to Detective Walker to investigate and discover who murdered mother and daughter. Meanwhile, Hannah will learn that the two women were patients at the Clinic to Heal the Mind in Lucerne, Switzerland, and she will take it upon herself to uncover the reason they were killed. Her search will lead her to the tranquil, remote town of Giethoorn in the Netherlands, where the trail ends at a secluded cabin Rafael brings her to — a place where the crucial answers are waiting.

Hannah will also learn that Christina hid yet another secret: that her husband Gonzalez was not her biological father, but rather Stu, a man whom Laura had loved at least once in her life. Will Hannah be able to determine who murdered Laura and what the secret was that led to her demise? The answer lie in The Thirteenth Riddle A Poisoned Silence.

title: My Journey as an Award-Winning Author
excerpt: If you had told me six years ago that I would be winning two awards at the IIBA and be nominated for Author of the Year in the True Crime category, I would not have believed you. I probably would…
html:
If you had told me six years ago that I would be winning two awards at the IIBA and be nominated for Author of the Year in the True Crime category, I would not have believed you. I probably would have laughed it off and said, “Me? You’re joking! My writing isn’t that good.” Growing up, I always loved writing. I had vivid imaginations, and when I went to college my passion for writing only deepened. I endured many professors who told me my work wasn’t good and that I should give up, but there was one man who believed in me — the same man who later inspired the character Rafael. When the pandemic hit in 2020, I realized I had to do something meaningful with my time, so I set about continuing my first novel, Deadly College Murders, the story of Hannah Walker and her godfather Rafael and their harrowing journey to uncover the truth behind the murders Hannah is accused of.

The one thing that I always experience on my writing journey is writer’s block. I cannot fathom how many times I have gone through it, and each occurrence feels both familiar and frustrating. But once I get over it, I fall into a steady rhythm and can write for hours at a stretch. From the very beginning I knew I wanted to create a mystery series, a layered set of stories that reward careful reading. For readers to fully appreciate the plots and character development, they need to take their time and read the books in order — beginning, of course, with Deadly College Murders, followed by Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes (Winner at the International Impact Book Awards 2026), and then Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession (Winner at the International Impact Book Awards 2025), which was also nominated for Author of the Year 2026 in the true crime category.

While I continue writing the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, including The Thirteenth Riddle, A Poisoned Silence, and Shadows of Her Past, I am also beginning a new series titled the Astrid Fitzgerald Mystery Series, starting with “Who Murdered Erica Ivy.” Astrid Fitzgerald will be markedly different from the Hannah Walker books. Where Hannah is portrayed as a long‑suffering protagonist, Astrid will be the opposite—cold, detached, and uncompromising in every way. Similarly, whereas Rafael is portrayed as deeply devoted to his beloved goddaughter, Thomas will serve as a foil to that dynamic. Thomas is Astrid’s former professor who offers counsel when she needs it, all the while concealing his true feelings for her.
seo_title: My Journey as an Award-Winning Author

title: Rafael Poisoned…
excerpt: Hannah and Rafael… the two protagonists who suffer at every turn. I knew I had to give more character development to Rafael. While Rafael was important in Deadly College Murders, that first book in…
html:
Hannah and Rafael… the two protagonists who suffer at every turn. I knew I had to give more character development to Rafael. While Rafael was important in Deadly College Murders, that first book in the series focused more on Hannah and her determination to discover who murdered Gonzalez. It also centered on the persistent premonition dreams she kept having, dreams that continue to haunt her regularly as the series progresses.

Going into the second book, I knew I wanted Rafael to undergo more development. How much did he change in the three years he spent traveling with his goddaughter? He grew wiser than he already was and became even more protective of Hannah. How was I going to ensure Rafael received more time and attention in the second book, similar to Hannah? By having Hannah lose her memory and forget who he was, I created an opportunity to explore the fears, hopes, and dreams Rafael carried for the future.

In Deadly Vows we explore the deep fears Rafael experiences when he discovers Hannah is losing her memory. The more he struggles and fights to make sure she remembers who he is, the less he sees that Hannah is quietly pushing him away. As her frustration boils over and she shouts that she will never remember him, Rafael’s hope collapses; distraught and defeated, he finally gives up and leaves her a heartbreaking letter.

Following the events of Deadly Vows and moving into Paris Noir Deadly Obsession, Rafael has moved on and has been undercover for six months—six long months during which Hannah did not see or hear from her beloved godfather. As Hannah prepares for her upcoming nuptials with Jonathan, Rafael remains unaware that his past is resurfacing to haunt him. An arch‑nemesis emerges who must upend the hero’s life; in this story, that hero is Rafael. He spends the entire book focused on keeping Hannah safe, driven by the consuming fear of losing her, until she finally confronts him with a hard truth: new threats arrive every day, and he cannot always shield her from danger.

After the events of Paris Noir, Hannah and Rafael are not exactly on speaking terms in The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence, their strained relationship marked by awkward silences and unspoken tensions.

When Rafael tries to calm Hannah’s attitude and anger, Hannah erupts into an explosive fight with him that ends with Rafael being kidnapped. As she learns of his abduction, an immense guilt overwhelms her—she remembers how she’d mostly yelled at him and said things she now deeply regrets. After she manages to rescue Rafael and breaks down in his arms in their New Orleans apartment, Hannah’s world darkens further: at the hospital they tell her the one thing she never wanted to hear. Her beloved godfather has been poisoned, and the only clues point to a place called Die Klinik Den Geist Zu Halen. Now Hannah must race to find the antidote that could save Rafael. The answers—and the dangers—lie in TTRAPS.

About Bree T. Wilson

Bree T. Wilson is a gripping thriller author whose work explores the devastating consequences of buried secrets and the violence that erupts when the past refuses to stay hidden.

Her writing weaves together psychological tension, intricate plotting, and deeply personal stakes to create stories that demand to be read in a single sitting.

title: Astrid Fitzgerald Mystery Series. Hannah Vs Astrid; Rafael vs Thomas.

Hannah Walker. A dedicated student with sharp curiosity and a keen eye, she aspires to emulate Sherlock Holmes. Accused of a series of murders at her college, she endures a period of disorienting memory loss before gradually recovering fragmented recollections — and now faces an uncertain future as she is set to be married.

Astrid Fitzgerald. A no-nonsense detective with a steely demeanor, she is tough, cold-hearted, and shaped by a painful past that has left her largely alone and guarded. The only man she trusts is her former professor who trained her to be a dedicated detective and taught her how to read people.

She has bad blood with Erica, since Erica ruined her life in the worst possible way years earlier; nonetheless, Thomas will make sure she keeps a clear head when she is sent to speak with Erica after Erica suffered a break-in.

Rafael Walker-Smith. A former cop turned professor and the godfather to Hannah Walker, he is fiercely protective and determined to steer Hannah away from destructive choices and the metaphorical oncoming trains he fears for her.

Thomas. A former cop and current professor who serves as Astrid’s trusted confidant, offering calm counsel and steady support.

However, he is not like Rafael. While Rafael tries to make sure that he pulls Hannah away from the path of oncoming trains, Thomas does not act in the same overt manner. He trusts that Astrid is strong and resilient, yet when the murder of Erica occurs he quietly implores her to keep a steady mind and not let the loss consume her. As the story moves forward, we will gradually learn more about Thomas — the depth of his concern for Astrid and the careful ways he conceals his feelings while still supporting her.

These are the main differences between Hannah/Astrid and Rafael/Thomas. The Astrid Fitzgerald Series will begin with the murder of Erica and will include a wide array of suspects, each with plausible motives and hidden secrets that will keep readers guessing about the identity of the true killer.

Readers will also learn what unfolded between Erica and Astrid many years earlier, revealing long-buried tensions and secrets. As the author, I will scatter numerous red herrings throughout this series, and much like the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, it will be up to attentive readers to track the nuances of each character. Only I know who is truly responsible for Erica’s murder.

title: Hannah’s memory loss and recovery
excerpt: After finishing Deadly College Murders, I knew I wanted to go big with Hannah. As I mentioned in my previous posts, many changes didn’t make it into the books, but one theme I was determined to…
html:
After finishing Deadly College Murders, I knew I wanted to go big with Hannah. As I mentioned in my previous posts, many changes didn’t make it into the books, but one theme I was determined to explore further was memory loss. As the protagonist of the books along with Rafael, the protagonist is always going to be the one who suffers.

What makes Deadly Vows so unique is how successful Hannah becomes. Initially she planned to live in New York, but I chose Paris as Hannah’s final destination instead. During the three years she spent in Europe with Rafael, Hannah rose to notable success in the fashion industry. Yet despite her achievements, the dreams continued to haunt her.

Nightmares of the reveal from Deadly College Murders continued, haunting her with vivid images of the faces of those who had ruined her life. When she returned to the States with Rafael, she found she couldn’t let Connie’s murder go unanswered. She felt compelled to ensure the truth was uncovered so Connie could finally receive the justice she deserved. After a frightening car accident, Rafael urged Hannah to be more careful and cautious, but she still chose to refuse his orders. Hannah’s determination was so fixated, that she chooses to travel to New Orleans to learn more on Sofia’s past (see DCM characters).

When she arrived at the apartment after speaking with Sofia’s former professor, she was immediately confronted by the person responsible for the senseless act. She had no idea that this encounter would alter the course of her life. When she later awakens in the hospital with Rafael at her bedside, he is stunned to discover that his beloved goddaughter cannot remember who he is. What follows is a painful effort: Rafael does everything he can to help Hannah reclaim her memory, but after a series of attempts she explodes at him, telling him to go to hell, and he ultimately decides to step back.

Why did I choose to have Hannah suffer from memory loss? The answer came to me on a road trip I took to find someone who had made a real impact on my life. I remember that day as if it were yesterday: I took the day off work and drove out to where he was at. As the miles passed, my mind was full of questions and nervous anticipation. During the drive I kept turning the same worries over in my head: “What if he doesn’t remember me? What if he’s lost his memory? If he has, how will I even begin to approach him?”

To my surprise he did remember me. We talked and the conversation settled something in me. On the drive home I couldn’t stop thinking about the story I wanted to tell and how that emotional encounter could be translated to fiction. That’s when it became clear Hannah should lose her memory — not because memory loss is dramatic on its own, but because of the unique kind of pain it would cause Rafael. Imagining how he would react, the confusion, the ache, the effort to hold onto someone slipping away, made those chapters necessary. Writing them was often draining; I would wake, eat, and then lose myself in the work for hours, rewriting scenes again and again until the emotions felt true.

The confrontation Hannah has with Rafael before the reveal was perhaps one of the most painful scenes I ever had to write. I had to tap not only into Hannah’s raw emotions and simmering anger and those around her, but also into the deep, complicated sorrow Rafael carried beneath his calm. The night was quiet and Hannah was wound tight with frustration toward Rafael, so much so that she finally tells him off — accusing him of everything: for the hooded figure finding them, for the fire in the cabin, for the fractures that followed. She explodes at him, yells at him, and lets loose all the fear and blame she has been holding in. Rafael chooses not to argue; he leaves and heads back to the apartment in silence. After he finishes packing, he pours himself into a heartbreaking letter to Hannah. The memories he shares are the key that forces Hannah to reclaim her own lost past: he writes about the time they set off to buy a mismatched tea set, the long walks along the Seine watching the Eiffel Tower’s lights sparkle at midnight, and the ways he comforted her through those three long years of nightmares and sleepless nights.

As Hannah enters the apartment and finds the letter, all those memories Rafael had warned her about begin to rush back into her head. She recognizes the full extent of the mistake she made and understands, with a sinking dread, that in the process she has put her godfather in danger. That realization builds into resolve, driving her toward the confrontation with the person who has been making her life a living hell and save her beloved godfather.

All in all, Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes is packed with mystery, suspense, and hair-raising chills at every turn. Intricate riddles and haunting dreams demand careful attention from readers as they piece together clues to uncover who is responsible for this new wave of killings. It is clear as to why DVEOCC won an International Impact Book Award!
seo_title: Hannah’s memory loss and recovery

title: The Thirteenth Riddle A Poisoned Silence… A Hannah Walker Mystery Series.
excerpt: The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence… A Hannah Walker Mystery Series follows the relentless pursuits of Detective Hannah Walker. Hannah, a woman once haunted by killer riddles, deadly vows, and…
html:
The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence… A Hannah Walker Mystery Series follows the relentless pursuits of Detective Hannah Walker. Hannah, a woman once haunted by killer riddles, deadly vows, and bloodied dresses, is now a cold-hearted, no-nonsense detective driven by a quiet, steely resolve.

After the events of Paris Noir, Hannah has no time for games or for pretending to be some kind of amateur Sherlock Holmes. Her relationship with Rafael has grown cold over the past couple of years, leaving an undercurrent of unease and a steady sense of distrust in everything he says and does. Still, despite the distance and the doubts, she cannot wholly let go—there remains a quiet, complicated care for him beneath the surface.

On top of that, Hannah is now a new mom to a baby girl named Shayla. Despite her tiny age, Shayla seems wise beyond her years and adores her mother, even though Hannah will soon head off to Europe in search of the antidote needed to save Rafael’s life.

What will make The Thirteenth Riddle stand out from the other books is the deepening bond between Hannah and Rafa — how their trust, tensions, and shared history are tested and transformed. How far will Hannah be willing to go to solve the case and save her godfather’s life?

What has happened with Rafa over the last couple of years after the events of Paris Noir? Rafael still works as a professor but this time from home, maintaining his courses and research remotely. He chose not to relocate, not wanting to leave Hannah alone, especially after the tense showdown in Paris all those years ago. The experience left both of them more cautious, so Rafa has focused on creating a stable, quieter life—balancing his academic responsibilities with the small, steady routines that help them both feel safer.

After learning that Gonzalez’s ex has been found murdered, Rafael becomes single-minded about Hannah’s safety and keeping her focused, but he can’t help noticing unsettling changes in his beloved goddaughter and realizes she is becoming a cold‑hearted detective. When he gently tries to reason with Hannah about the direction she’s taking, their conversation escalates into a tense argument — and the confrontation takes a darker turn when Rafael is abducted.

After she learns her beloved godfather has been kidnapped, Hannah goes rogue and finds a way to rescue him, navigating danger and deception with a fierce, determined clarity she hadn’t known she possessed. Once she manages to get him free, the adrenaline finally drains away and she collapses into his arms, sobbing as she apologizes for the coldness and distance she’s shown him. She confesses that the horrific events in Paris all those years ago left her deeply traumatized, and that fear of losing him has made her push him away instead of holding on. She cries for hours in his embrace, letting out the pain she’s carried alone, and eventually, exhausted, falls asleep clinging to him. The next day Rafael is rushed to the hospital, and Hannah faces a gut‑wrenching truth: he has been poisoned. The only hope for an antidote lies somewhere in Lucerne, at a place called Die Klinik den Geist Zu Halen—the clinic to heal the mind—or, in some cases, to erase minds for good.

The love she feels for her godfather drives Hannah to do the unthinkable: she ingests the very toxin that is already coursing through his veins. With both of them poisoned, their only hope rests with a doctor named Stu, whose tangled past with Gonzalez’s ex-wife holds the crucial clue to an antidote that could save Hannah and Rafael. As the poison takes hold, Hannah is tormented by vivid dreams and haunting visions: a long hallway of mirrors reflecting fractured, distorted versions of herself; a ghostly train roaring through a thick, impenetrable fog with faceless passengers staring blankly; and a small tea table where Christina’s trembling hand reveals a hidden key beneath a shattered cup. Each dream arrives like a fragment of a puzzle — part clue, part warning — pushing Hannah closer to the truth and the race for a cure.

Will Hannah be able to save Rafael? Will she find the truth she is looking for? Or will The Thirteenth Riddle be her last? The answers lie in: The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence

novel explores the fragile line between love and suspicion, safety and betrayal.

The inspiration behind Pair Noir: Deadly Obsession lies in the enduring fascination with how unresolved truths can

shape the present. Wilson weaves themes of justice, identity, and redemption into a narrative that keeps readers

that resonates beyond its thrilling plot.

This book is ideal for readers who enjoy psychological thrillers, romantic suspense, and strong female protagonists

Bree T. Wilson is an emerging author known for crafting suspenseful stories that explore the complexities of human

filled with unexpected turns. With this release, she continues to establish herself as a voice to watch in contemporary

thriller fiction.

As secrets unravel and the truth comes into focus, Pair Noir: Deadly Obsession delivers a powerful reminder that the
