title: A chance encounter with an illusionist
excerpt: I always like to incorporate my real-life experiences into my books. The same can be said for Paris Noir, where nothing is quite as it appears and the lines of obsession blur past the point of…
html:
I always like to incorporate my real-life experiences into my books. The same can be said for Paris Noir, where nothing is quite as it appears and the lines of obsession blur past the point of delusion. After Rafael is run down on the very day she is meant to be married, Hannah and her companions come to realize that the answers they seek are tied to the hidden stream in Las Vegas—the same secretive place Hannah visited in 2019 before Gonzalez destroyed her by harassing her and turning the college against her.

Like myself, Hannah loves magic, and it’s the one thing Rafael can never seem to comprehend about his goddaughter. He just doesn’t understand why she adores traveling to Las Vegas to take in a dazzling magic show. Hannah, however, gently reminds Rafael that sometimes the people you meet along the way—strangers, fellow travelers, or performers—might turn out to be the person who changes your life in a meaningful, positive way.

When Hannah arrives in Las Vegas, she tells Bree, Jonathan, and Rafael that she plans to go see Angel perform in his Mindfreak show. While seated in the front row, Hannah has a striking encounter with his illusionist, the woman who flies away with Criss while he levitates, and immediately senses that this performer could alter the course of her life for the better. After the ninety-minute spectacle, Hannah and the others make their way to Gordon Ramsay’s Hell’s Kitchen for dinner. Later, as Hannah re-enters the hotel — briefly separated from Rafael — she runs into Tatiana, the stunning illusionist from the performance. Hannah praises her and tells her how much she loved the act. At the airport, fate brings Hannah and Tatiana together again, and Hannah impulsively invites her to the wedding. Like Hannah, Tatiana changed my life in unexpected ways and reminded me that life is beautiful; sometimes a single chance encounter with one person is enough to change everything for the better. How will Tatiana impact Hannah’s life? To not reveal much, let’s just say Tatiana will arrive in the nick of time, just when Hannah needs it the most.

In the Thirteenth Riddle, Tatiana is now living her best life after many years on stage, turning her attention to giving thought-provoking TED talks, all while caring tenderly for her goddaughter Shayla and continuing to support Hannah in meaningful ways.
seo_title: A chance encounter with an illusionist

title: Hannah and Jonathan’s love story is full of passion and challenges, but will they make it through and finally say “I do?”
excerpt: Hannah meets Jonathan in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. Jonathan is a private investigator, and from the very moment they meet, Hannah feels an unexpected spark between them. Still…
html:
Hannah meets Jonathan in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. Jonathan is a private investigator, and from the very moment they meet, Hannah feels an unexpected spark between them. Still, Hannah—true to herself—wants to keep her distance and avoid getting emotionally involved with him.

After she returns to the States for Connie’s wedding, Hannah encounters a handsome stranger named Jonathan. She is understandably wary, especially given everything that happened to her three years earlier. When the hooded figure coerces a victim into tampering with Hannah’s brakes, she is caught in a horrific and massive car crash. As she slowly regains consciousness, she meets this stranger again, and their initial acquaintance deepens: what begins as a tentative friendship gradually blossoms into more tender feelings. Tragically, when Hannah travels to New Orleans to investigate Sofia’s past, she once again crosses paths with the would-be killer, who brutally assaults her and leaves her in a coma. When Hannah wakes with Rafael at her bedside, he is devastated to learn that his dearly loved goddaughter has lost her memory.

After Jonathan learns of this, he understands he must be patient with her and give her time. He’s quietly confident that, with care and the unfolding truth, she will gradually regain her memory. As the weeks go by and the investigation into Connie’s death and the details of Hannah’s past come to light, Hannah slowly begins to feel something for Jonathan again, and his hope grows that her memories will return. When Hannah explodes at Rafael, blaming him for their near-death experience and accusing him of causing the danger they faced, Jonathan moves to reach her emotionally. He keeps speaking gently and persistently, trying to break through the fog that clouds her mind. Eventually his steady words penetrate, and as Hannah reads Rafael’s letter, a sudden clarity returns — she remembers who he is. Overcome, she confesses to Jonathan that she feels tremendous guilt for what she did, convinced she had acted wrongly; Jonathan comforts her, explaining that her reaction was natural given that she had no recollection of him at the time.

After the reveal, Hannah awakens and, blinking in confusion, asks Rafael and Jonathan who they are. Worried she might be suffering from amnesia again, she masks her fear with a nervous grin and jokes that her sense of humor has returned. As Hannah and the others make their way back to Paris, Jonathan quietly plans a romantic proposal at the foot of the Eiffel Tower, and there she softly answers, “Yes.”

In Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, the couple is planning their wedding in Paris to begin their new life together. After Rafael is run down by a mysterious hooded figure, Hannah and the others return to the United States to investigate Rafael’s past and uncover how it is tied to Hannah’s own history.

Along the way, Hannah discovers she is pregnant and then suffers devastating rejection from Jonathan. Concerned that Jonathan may be under pressure or being blackmailed by someone, Rafael quietly launches his own investigation to uncover the truth. As they prepare to leave the States, Hannah encounters Tatiana, an illusionist from Las Vegas, and kindly invites her to the wedding. As Hannah prepares to say “I do,” she is once again disturbed by recurring dreams in which she never gets to speak those two words. Will the haunting visions Hannah has been having come true? Or will she and Jonathan find their way to the happy ending they both crave? The answer lies in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession.
seo_title: Hannah and Jonathan’s Love Story: Will They Say “I Do”?

title: Mason, an antagonist driven by an intense desire for revenge against Hannah.
excerpt: Paris Noir is filled with intriguing new characters. One character I especially enjoyed writing was Mason. Mason is an officer from Las Vegas, toughened by the city’s grit and committed to justice.…
html:
Paris Noir is filled with intriguing new characters. One character I especially enjoyed writing was Mason. Mason is an officer from Las Vegas, toughened by the city’s grit and committed to justice. When he learns that a string of murders has been occurring back home, Mason quickly fixes his attention on Hannah. But who is this driven man, and what fuels the intensity of his desire?

That answer lies solely with one man: Rafael Walker-Smith. From the very beginning of the series, I knew I wanted Rafael to carry a past that would eventually come back to haunt him. During his years on the force, Rafael unearthed disturbing secrets tied to a fellow officer, Donovan, and the more he learned the clearer it became that Donovan was compromised. As Rafael dug deeper, he discovered that Mason was the shadowy figure covering up Donovan’s dirty work, a man who believed he had kept his personal affairs tightly sealed. Mason is stunned to learn that Rafael has a goddaughter—Hannah Walker—whom Rafael had not been in contact with for years, a fact that fractures the fragile balance between them and sets the stage for the tensions to come.

When he leaves the force to begin a new life as a college professor, Mason warns Rafael that one day he will make good on a promise: he intends to hurt the one person Rafael loves most—his goddaughter. Mason says that if Rafael ever missteps and he happens to cross paths with Hannah, he will not hesitate to see her jailed, purely to watch Rafael suffer. After finding multiple bodies in Las Vegas that the hooded figure commits, Mason doesn’t hesitate to arrest Hannah. After her arrest, she calls Rafael and tells her the situation she is going through.

As she sits in the interrogation room, Mason dives deeply into Hannah’s past and promises that he will see to it she goes to jail permanently — and that he will make sure the sentence holds. Hannah begs him to leave her and Rafael alone, but Mason refuses; he vows he will not rest until Rafael pays for what he’s done. Hannah reads Mason like an open book and speaks the truth without hesitation: he hates Rafael because he could not accept that Rafael was a good cop, and he resented that Rafael would not join him in framing innocent people.

Hannah also uncovers that Mason is in cahoots with Donovan and learns they will stop at nothing to ensure that the wedding in Paris doesn’t take place. Realizing the danger and how deeply the conspiracy runs, Hannah calls upon Smith and asks him to arrest her so she can infiltrate their circle and learn more about Donovan, Mason, and Bree. Mason, in particular, reminds me of a man I met many years ago — the kind of person who, from the moment I first saw him, gave me the unmistakable sense that he was likely not to be trusted.
seo_title: Mason: An Antagonist Driven by Revenge

title: Rafael uncovers Hannah’s darkest secrets.
excerpt: Rafael and Hannah. An unlikely duo, bound by circumstance and stubborn resolve. The true protagonists of the series, they carry the story’s weight through danger and doubt. Two people fighting…
html:
Rafael and Hannah. An unlikely duo, bound by circumstance and stubborn resolve. The true protagonists of the series, they carry the story’s weight through danger and doubt. Two people fighting against the malevolent forces of frame, murder, and dark secrets that threaten to unravel everything they hold dear. A key element the reader must watch for is that, since the start of the second book, not everything is what it appears to be.

Just as Rafael keeps certain things to himself, Hannah harbors her own secrets as well. Coincidentally, at the beginning of Paris Noir, Rafael pays Hannah a visit and immediately notices how visibly tense she has become. She confides in him about the puzzling riddle that was handed to her and recounts how a mysterious man warned that both she and Rafael are in imminent danger. He scolds his goddaughter, insisting that she must be truthful with him and promising to do the same in return — an ironic demand, given that Rafa is concealing a dark past from Hannah precisely to try to protect her from harm.

During the period that Hannah is under house arrest, she asks Smith for help in arranging her arrest so she can finally learn who a certain someone really is. While these events unfold in Las Vegas, Rafael is back in Paris investigating the murder of a police officer who once knew Hannah. When he arrives at the crime scene, he discovers a letter from Hannah and learns that much of what he believed was merely a cover staged during her recovery period. Troubled by why she kept this from him, Rafael decides to return to Las Vegas to confront his beloved. Before he has the chance to question her face to face, Hannah reveals parts of her plan and explains that Smith will be the one to take her into custody. Rather than reveal his knowledge or warn her, Rafael chooses to remain silent and intends to confront her later in jail.

When he finally does confront her, he asks her why she hid this important factor from him. She once again reminds him that he cannot keep pulling her from the path of oncoming trains, and that what she did, she did to protect him, to make sure Donovan wouldn’t kill him. She tells him that if anything were to happen to him, she would never forgive herself, because that is how much she loves him. Not only does she love him dearly, she is extremely loyal to him, to the point that if she were ever forced to choose between Rafael and Jonathan, she would choose Rafael first without a doubt. Keep an eye out for the letter Hannah wrote to Rafael while she sat in a cafe in Paris three years ago; the clues to what she was really working on are tucked away in that letter.
seo_title: Rafael uncovers Hannah’s darkest secrets.

title: Rafael, the center of Hannah’s universe.
excerpt: Hannah’s heart has room for everyone who meets her. Tatiana, the stunning and gorgeous former illusionist who will become a huge part of Hannah’s life and whose presence brings both mystery and…
html:
Hannah’s heart has room for everyone who meets her. Tatiana, the stunning and gorgeous former illusionist who will become a huge part of Hannah’s life and whose presence brings both mystery and warmth. Jonathan, the man she fell deeply in love with and is now set to marry, promising a future full of hope. Smith… the once antagonistic detective who slowly shifts into a complicated, begrudging ally. But none of these characters could top the enormous love she feels for Rafael. For Hannah, Rafael is the steady center of her universe. Time and time again, from the very start of the first book and continuing through the third, Rafael has proven how profoundly he loves his goddaughter and how far he is willing to go to keep her safe and cared for.

Similar to Paris Noir, he will once again be at the center of the action in The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence. At the start of the fourth book, she and Rafael are sharply at odds; he senses her anger and does his best—gentle words, concerned gestures—to urge her to calm down, but his efforts prove fruitless. Echoing DVEOCC, the heated, sprawling argument she has with Raf becomes a decision she comes to rue, especially once she discovers, to her horror, that he has been poisoned.

It will fall to Hannah in A Poisoned Silence to discover who is responsible for the poisoning of her beloved godfather. Her love for him is so immense that she will take the reckless, heartbreaking step of ingesting the very same toxin coursing through his veins, a desperate, audacious attempt to piece together the truth and buy him time—no matter the personal cost.

With the sands of time running low, Hannah and Rafael set out together on a fragile, beautiful journey to track down the antidote that could save them both. Along the way, Hannah begins once more to be haunted by visions of a strange carnival, where she is forced to take part in a tense game of chance that may lead her to the cure and to the rescue of her godfather. In this tale of poisoned silence, fate hangs precariously in the balance—there is only a fifty–fifty chance that he will live or die.
seo_title: Rafael, the center of Hannah’s universe.

title: Why the hidden stream is such an important element in Paris Noir
excerpt: As the events of Paris Noir begin to unfold, there is a key factor that weaves through the series… the hidden stream. It is beside this secluded waterway that Hannah is often able to uncover the…
html:
As the events of Paris Noir begin to unfold, there is a key factor that weaves through the series… the hidden stream. It is beside this secluded waterway that Hannah is often able to uncover the answers she seeks. Whether she deciphers a riddle left by the killer or simply needs a place of solace and quiet reflection, the stream consistently plays an important and quietly powerful role, offering both clues and calm when the world around her is chaotic.

After she is shot in Las Vegas and begins the slow, painful process of recovery, Hannah reaches out to Bree and asks her to join the stream, convinced that its currents hold the answers she needs and the focus required to piece together scattered memories. It is during this broadcast, amid the quiet of convalescence and the rush of memory, that Hannah begins to recall how the events of 2019 unfolded. She is constantly dreaming of this stream and she knows that it is here, in that familiar bend of water, that she can find what she is looking for and reclaim the fragments of her past.

Eventually, during a private moment, Rafael tells Hannah how he recollected that one event and told her that story as she was laying in a coma in Deadly Vows, a revelation that deepens the link between them. As the past catches up to Rafael, we begin to understand why his role carries such weight in the series: his memories and choices shape much of what Hannah must confront. When she was little, Hannah ran away from home; along the way she stumbled across a hidden stream where Rafael eventually found her, a meeting that set into motion consequences felt throughout their lives.

As you begin reading the three books, be sure to watch carefully for the subtle clues that point toward the perpetrator; they’re tucked away in these small but significant moments.
seo_title: Why the hidden stream is such an important element in Paris Noir

title: From Paris to Venice, Florence, and Rome: the European adventures of Hannah and Raf.
excerpt: A recurring theme in the series is Hannah and her growing obsession with travel and the freedom it promises. While she lay in jail, she repeatedly imagined her future liberty and made plans in her…
html:
A recurring theme in the series is Hannah and her growing obsession with travel and the freedom it promises. While she lay in jail, she repeatedly imagined her future liberty and made plans in her mind for everything she would do the moment she walked out. Indeed, one of the very first trips Hannah took after her release was to the Cayman Islands, a brief escape that fed her wanderlust. After she solved the murder of the theatre actress and boarded the plane with Daniel, she felt certain she wanted to leave the States behind and embrace a new life in Europe. Though the story was originally set to conclude in New York, I shifted the narrative to move Hannah to Paris, inspired by my own travels and experiences there in 2023.

After her tense confrontation with the suspect in the first book, Rafael makes a solemn, heartfelt promise to Hannah that he will protect her, and he gently reminds her that if she needs anything at all, she should never hesitate to let him know. Sure enough, when Hannah begins to crave something new and different, she asks Raf to whisk her away on a spontaneous European adventure. Between the events of the first book and the second, Hannah spends three full, exhilarating years living and exploring life across Europe—immersing herself in new cities, cultures, and friendships—until Connie calls and asks her to fly home for her wedding. For Hannah, leaving Europe behind again is every bit as bittersweet and wrenching as it was the first time.

In the upcoming fourth book, after her godfather is poisoned, Hannah tells Smith she will be taking a sabbatical and plans to travel to Lucerne to stay at Die Klinik Dan Geist Zu Halen. She also tells him she intends to take Rafael on a European adventure, much like the one Rafael once gave her. So Hannah and Raf set off together, first exploring the ruins of the Colosseum, where gladiators once fought and Christians were persecuted, then wandering through the ancient remains of the Forum and learning how it came into being in the 6th century BC. Before continuing their journey, Hannah and Raf climb up to the dome of St. Peter’s Basilica to take in the sweeping lights of the Eternal City, then stroll along Via Condotti, ascend the Spanish Steps and throw coins into the Fontana di Trevi. Their travels carry them next to the romantic canals of Venice, where Hannah and Rafael glide through the water on a gondola. They then move on to Paris, where their story first began—holding hands as she watches the city’s flashing lights at midnight and walking along the banks of the Seine. Shortly afterward they travel to Florence, where they enjoy a meal at Osteria Pastella and savor more moments together.

In the TTRAPS, Rafael takes Hannah to the beautiful, peaceful town of Giethoorn. Ironically nicknamed the “Venice of the Netherlands,” this story is set in a picturesque village whose canals, thatched roofs, and quiet footbridges will take Hannah by surprise and enchant her senses. (Though I have never been to Giethoorn or Lucerne, I hope to go there someday.)
seo_title: The European Adventures of Hannah and Raf

title: Smith… the minor recurring character
excerpt: If you have had the chance to read my book, you know that more than likely you hated Smith. Especially the way he and Frigon treated Hannah. Since they made their appearance in the debut novel Deadly…
html:
If you have had the chance to read my book, you know that more than likely you hated Smith. Especially the way he and Frigon treated Hannah. Since they made their appearance in the debut novel Deadly College Murders, Smith was initially convinced Hannah was guilty. The more he would run into her, at the crime scenes, the more suspicious he became of her. When she goes to the scene of the crime where the psychology professor has been murdered, he is happy that he gets to arrest her. But after Hannah was convicted and sentenced to death (before the judge learned that she was pregnant) he becomes convinced that this college student was telling him the truth, and that she is not guilty.

Once Hannah is released, she tells Smith that when she uncovers who is behind the murders, she will call him so he can take credit for arresting the culprit. After the suspect is apprehended and brought to justice, Smith offers Hannah a job on the force as a rookie; although she appreciates the opportunity and is flattered by the offer, she gently declines, explaining that she needs time to heal both psychologically and emotionally before taking on a new commitment.

Smith next makes his appearance in Deadly Vows Echoes of College Crimes, this time warning Hannah that she must stay away from the current case for her own safety — he insists he does not want her to get hurt, signaling that the rivalry he once felt toward her has been left firmly in the past. After Hannah is attacked by the hooded figure and subsequently loses her memory, Smith steps in to support Rafael and the others, assisting their investigation from a distance until he eventually comes to the safe house. When Hannah later recovers her memory after reading Rafael’s letter, she calls Smith to tell him who the culprit is and to let him know that her memories have returned.

In Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession he once again finds himself at the heart of the investigation that Hannah and the team are pursuing. He becomes the person who will arrange for Hannah to be placed in jail (at her own request) as a way to uncover the truth about who Bree really is. Though he resists the plan at first, he ultimately tells Hannah he trusts her judgment and that his priority is ensuring she comes out of the situation unharmed. Smith will be the one to confront and bring the killer to justice during the climactic showdown in the church, and he will also have the opportunity to save a life—but which life will he ultimately spare? Hannah’s or Jonathan’s?

In the upcoming fourth book, titled The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence, Hannah is now working alongside Smith, who will play a pivotal role in keeping her steady and preventing her from going off the rails. Smith is modeled after Psych’s lead detective Carlton Lassiter, bringing a grounded, no-nonsense presence to Hannah’s world.
seo_title: Smith… the minor recurring character

title: The Hooded Figure: A Psychological Mastermind
excerpt: The Hooded Figure. The number one mastermind in the series… and Hannah and Rafa’s most dangerous nemesis. Always concealed, this mysterious figure wears a dark hooded jacket, gloves, and carries…
html:
The Hooded Figure. The number one mastermind in the series… and Hannah and Rafa’s most dangerous nemesis. Always concealed, this mysterious figure wears a dark hooded jacket, gloves, and carries knives or guns. They are the catalyst who alters Hannah’s outlook on life, driving her into a new, darker reality. Beginning with Deadly College Murders, the Hooded Figure could be anyone—someone with inside access to faculty records and class schedules, moving unseen through the campus while pulling strings from the shadows.

He or she is the one who works closely with the series’ main antagonist. They are responsible for orchestrating evidence and false leads to ensure Hannah is framed for every crime they commit. Typically, an early riser, they’re often up before 5 a.m., eager to begin the day and take deliberate steps to guarantee the murders occur as planned.

Under direct orders from the main antagonist, they are the ones who send Hannah and Raf the riddles. If either of them answers a riddle incorrectly, the consequence is severe: it results in the possible demise of Hannah or Rafael, or both.

Hannah often dreams of the hooded figure murdering her and Rafael, a recurring nightmare that leaves her unsettled long after she wakes. Some of the villains in the book subject Hannah to psychological torture, probing her fears and unraveling her sense of safety. It might be someone she once trusted as her closest friend, or it could be a stranger whose sinister nature she gradually uncovers through small, chilling clues.

The hooded figure is the one responsible for ensuring Hannah goes to jail; if their plan falters, they find other ways to try to make certain she ends up behind bars. All in all, the hooded figure will always be one step ahead of Hannah. It falls to her and Rafael to play this dangerous game of chess. One thing Hannah remembers often, though not always clearly, is that…

“In life unlike chess, the game continues after checkmate.”
seo_title: The Hooded Figure: A Psychological Mastermind

title: A tolling bell, a frantic run through the woods, a sudden loss of memory, and a bloodied wedding dress… these haunting dreams carry deep significance for Hannah throughout the books.
excerpt: A recurring theme in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, from its very beginning, has been the vivid dreams that Hannah experiences. When I created the character, I wanted her to possess a particular…
html:
A recurring theme in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, from its very beginning, has been the vivid dreams that Hannah experiences. When I created the character, I wanted her to possess a particular, almost uncanny gift, and those dreams became a central element of her identity. A piece of advice I give readers is to pay close attention to the details in Hannah’s dreams, because often those images and sensations are the subtle clues that will ultimately guide them toward uncovering the killer. Hannah is a layered, complicated protagonist who strives to be the best version of herself despite numerous setbacks. Time and time again she crosses paths with people who betray her or reveal themselves to be downright malevolent. One pattern I noticed early on is how specific encounters trigger recurring dream sequences: after meeting certain characters, Hannah will fall asleep and find herself sprinting down a deserted hallway, only to be shot at the far end while a bell tolls; in other instances she is haunted by visions of the person responsible in the first book—phantom figures racing through moonlit woods—images that linger long after she wakes.

The sudden loss of memory played a major role in shaping Hannah’s character. As the protagonist, she endures real hardship. When I began writing the second book I kept asking myself, “What could I do to Hannah that will deeply affect every character she encounters?” I thought, “Wouldn’t it be powerful if Hannah suffered even more by losing her memory?” Even after that loss, she still experiences fractured premonition dreams from before the amnesia, and those visions ultimately help her solve the final clue and save Rafael.

A bloodied wedding dress. The very image of the wedding Hannah wonders whether she will ever have. At the start of the third book Hannah is blissful—she is about to marry the love of her life—until Rafael is struck down. As the story unfolds, she is tormented by a recurring nightmare in which Jonathan is shot and her wedding gown is soaked in blood. Moving forward, I will explore Hannah’s backstory and the origins of her premonitory dreams in greater depth.
seo_title: Hannah’s Haunting Dreams and What They Mean

title: Why Rafael had to confront his past in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession
excerpt: Rafael… a complicated, layered man. Modeled in part after my former professor, the recollections I held of him helped shape the character of Rafael Walker-Smith. When we first encounter Rafael in…
html:
Rafael… a complicated, layered man. Modeled in part after my former professor, the recollections I held of him helped shape the character of Rafael Walker-Smith. When we first encounter Rafael in Deadly College Murders, he has only just reentered his goddaughter’s life. Fiercely protective where Hannah is concerned, she represents his greatest vulnerability—his Achilles’ heel. If anything were to befall her, he knows he could never forgive himself. The first two books in the series, Deadly College Murders and Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes, focused on Hannah, with Rafael playing an important and emotionally charged role throughout, albeit not always.

In writing the third book in the series, I wanted it to focus squarely on Rafael and how his dark past comes back to haunt him. The sins of the godfather return to threaten everything he has built in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession. He is a man doing his utmost to protect his beloved goddaughter, and an arch-nemesis must upend the hero’s life — in this case, Rafael faces Donovan, a man from his past who resurfaces to terrorize him and to target the one person Rafael cares for most: Hannah. Donovan cheated the criminal justice system and was corrupt from the start; when Rafael exposed him to his superiors, Donovan vowed revenge and bided his time. Hannah, meanwhile, is Rafael’s precious gem.

It is Rafael’s hidden history and his determination to keep Donovan from finding her that ultimately strain the bond between godfather and goddaughter. Ironically, at the start of the third book Rafael insists Hannah must always tell him the truth, warning that secrecy can be more damaging than honesty — all while he conceals his own darkest secrets to keep her safe. Our pasts shape who we are, and Rafael is no exception. Near the end of the book he discovers what Hannah has been hiding since the aftermath of Deadly College Murders and during the events between Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. When he confronts her, she reveals that he lied about his identity to protect her, and that she, too, lied to protect herself. How the ending of Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession alters Rafael and Hannah’s lives — and whether they can finally bring Donovan down — becomes the story’s central, tense resolution.
seo_title: Why Rafael had to confront his past in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession

title: Character Profile: Tatiana
excerpt: Tatiana, the stunning and captivating illusionist whom Hannah encounters in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, plays a pivotal role in both the first half of the book and again near its conclusion. She…
html:
Tatiana, the stunning and captivating illusionist whom Hannah encounters in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, plays a pivotal role in both the first half of the book and again near its conclusion. She becomes the person who helps Hannah begin to see life from a different perspective, showing her that with focus and determination, almost anything you set your mind to can be accomplished. Tatiana is also the lone witness when the final showdown unfolds in the church in Paris, and she later returns in the fourth book, The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence, as the godmother to Hannah’s daughter. Through her gentle insistence and daring example, Tatiana teaches Hannah that life doesn’t always have to be about chasing shadows or constantly running; sometimes it’s about the people you meet along the way and the moments that simply feel right. The right person can change you, Tatiana shows Hannah, reminding her that life is short and that “eventually” rarely arrives unless you make things happen.

She is someone who, the moment Hannah meets her, knows she will change her life for the better. Tatiana is the woman to whom my books are dedicated. She is always cheering me on and offering wise advice when I need it most; she is my trainer and life coach, and I am honored to include her in the third and fourth books respectively. After the events of Paris Noir Deadly Obsession we learn that she has left her life as an illusionist behind and is focusing solely on caring for her goddaughter and continues to offer advice to Hannah along the way.
seo_title: Character Profile: Tatiana

title: Why the connection between Raf and Hannah is unbreakable
excerpt: When I first started writing my debut novel, I knew Hannah would be the kind of person who discovers she doesn’t need anyone else to feel loved or cherished. She has built a life of her own and…
html:
When I first started writing my debut novel, I knew Hannah would be the kind of person who discovers she doesn’t need anyone else to feel loved or cherished. She has built a life of her own and carries herself as a strong-willed, fiercely independent woman. All of those shifts, however, when she is accused of the college murders. Suddenly she feels isolated and vulnerable, yet her godfather Rafael remains steadfastly at her side. One thing readers will notice is the deep, almost instinctive bond between godfather and goddaughter — an unbreakable connection that endures even in the face of memory loss. In future books I plan to explore more fully how Rafael’s return throws Hannah into an even lonelier place: she has no one else, and her ingrained independence makes her reluctant to ask for help or admit she needs protection, until Rafael reappears and upends that self-reliance. When we first meet Hannah she is secretly in contact with her godfather, who teaches at the college she attends, but she keeps their relationship hidden because she fears being accused of receiving special treatment. The character of Rafael is inspired by my former professor, R.G.; after years in his classroom, I wanted Rafael to carry a dark past — a history he desperately tries to conceal because he fears Hannah would be hurt if she ever learned the truth.

Despite the events of the second book and the accident that robs her of her memory, the bond between them endures, if altered. He tries his hardest to be understanding and patient, yet remains the steady, composed presence he has always been, until she acts in a way that forces him to make the painful decision to walk away.

In the third one, he is the main subject of Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession. When a man from his past resurfaces, Rafael grows increasingly fearful for Hannah’s safety, despite her pattern of constant accidents; when the roles reverse, Hannah remains steadfastly by her godfather’s side, proving that not even a loss of memory or a poisoned kidnapping can sever the unbreakable bond between them.

As the book progresses, Raf grows increasingly protective of her, to the point that she finally confronts her godfather and tells him, “You cannot keep pulling me from the path of oncoming trains.” She means that no matter how hard Rafael tries, he cannot shield her from every danger; new trains appear every day, and some risks she must face on her own. None the less nothing will stop the bond between these two, not even a poisoned silence.
seo_title: Why the connection between Raf and Hannah is unbreakable

title: Deadly College Murders: The Original Ending
excerpt: When I began writing my book Deadly College Murders in 2019, it took a great deal of courage for me to decide that I wanted my work to be published… someday. I waited patiently for five years while…
html:
When I began writing my book Deadly College Murders in 2019, it took a great deal of courage for me to decide that I wanted my work to be published… someday. I waited patiently for five years while the story and my confidence slowly took shape. Early on, before I finished the manuscript, I had an original ending in mind for Hannah: after uncovering who was behind the Deadly College Murders and learning the truth about what had happened to her, she was going to move to New York to work in fashion. Everything shifted, though, during a trip to Paris in November 2023. I was completely mesmerized by the city’s lights, the French culture, and the simple pleasure of eating a warm crêpe, and those impressions changed my vision for Hannah. In the end I chose Paris as her final destination, where she would begin a new chapter of her life alongside her godfather, Rafael.

In the original ending, Hannah was also going to end up with her best friend Daniel, but I changed it so the character would learn a meaningful lesson and so Hannah could show readers—especially female readers—that one does not need a man to feel complete. I drew some inspiration from General Hospital, specifically the storyline where Bobby fell for Noah Drake; Noah rejected her, and only when she was getting married did he realize he had let her slip through his fingers. Eventually Hannah and Rafael end up going to Paris, where Rafael will help her heal from the trauma she endured.
seo_title: Deadly College Murders: The Original Ending

title: How I came to be an Author
excerpt: If you would have told me 6 years ago that my 3rd book Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession would win at the International Impact Book Awards I would not have believed you. To tell you the story of how my…
html:
If you would have told me 6 years ago that my 3rd book Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession would win at the International Impact Book Awards I would not have believed you. To tell you the story of how my third book won, we have to go back to 2018.

2018 was a tough year for me, I was in college. Had the best CJ professor, the coolest who Rafael is mirrored after. Unfortunately I suffered for 10 months due to an invisible illness known as Endometriosis. When I was at the hospital, I began to think a lot about everything that I had been through for ten months. Right there and then I said to myself “I am going to pick up a hobby.” And then 2019 came.

I still remember it to this day. I was at the entrance of the library and I ran into one of my former classmates. Earlier in the year I had seen her looking at schools for dance. Me being nosy, saw her eyeing NYFA, then I told her that Juilliard was a better fit for her. Well, when I ran into her, she told me she had gotten accepted at Juilliard. Never had I ever felt so happy.

Since I was in between classes, after we said our goodbyes, I went deep into the library. As I sat down I started thinking “Wouldn’t it be interesting if there was a murder in the college and I could solve the case?” Be like Sherlock Holmes is what I was aspiring to be. The story itself underwent a lot of character name changes, characters I knew were not going to be relevant. Of course. I had to have a love interest. And then I chose to add Hannah’s godfather Rafael. Spending a lot of time with my professor in his classes is what helped me shape Rafael’s overprotective nature.

But then the pandemic hit. While we were in shut down, I started binge watching Forensic Files, Murder She Baked Mysteries with Alison Sweeney and Cameron Mathison. Crossword Mysteries with Lacey Chabert and Brennan Elliott and Aurora Teagarden mysteries starring Candace Cameron Bure. I started jotting down ideas, what I could take out, what I could add. There are so many stuff that I originally wrote, that eventually I left out. When it came to the ending, I got the idea while I was out with my mom. I started thinking about the twists and turns that could be featured in the final showdown between Hannah and the culprit.

Once I got a job, it did not stop me from continuing to write. I kept writing, sometimes I would get home at 7pm and would start writing for hours. It became a dedication, I wanted the book to be perfect. As the years passed by, I was determined to turn this book into the Hannah Walker Mystery Series. While I was writing Deadly College Murders, I started jotting down ideas for Deadly Vows Echoes of College Crimes. Initially titled: Wedding and a Murder, sequel to Deadly College Murders, the story follows Hannah returning to her hometown for her best friend’s wedding, only to be found dead before she said “I do.” I felt that, the more I wrote, the more I wanted to continue. Yes I was majoring in Criminal Justice, but I saw myself writing as well. Writing has always been my passion, many of my college professors would say that I was never going to amount to anything, and that I was not a good writer, well I proved them wrong. Only one man actually believed in me, and never brought me down, three guesses who R.G.

As I started writing Deadly Vows, I started jotting down ideas for the third book. Who would have thought that this third book was going to win at the International Impact Book Awards! Originally titled Paris Noir: Secrets of the past, I knew I wanted it to focus solely on Rafael. Then one day while on Instagram, I saw an ad for International Impact Book Awards! I decided to submit my three manuscripts. Of the 3 Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession is the one that won. My heart sank with emotion when I got the email! Thanks to the IIBA I now know fully that my dreams are valid, especially after so many people tried to diminish them. After receiving my trophy, I went to the Gala on Feb 27th! It was there that someone at my table asked me a question “What is your career?” and I said “Writing is my career.” Thank you to the incredible Nim Stant who inspired me to submit my book for consideration. I want to let everyone know that your dreams are valid and that if after reading this blog post, you get inspired to write your own book, whether it be mystery or romance, then I know that I have done my job. Nim Stant’s life story is mesmerizing. Remember that only YOU are in charge of writing your own path.
seo_title: How I came to be an Author

title: The most heartbreaking thing to write was Rafael’s letter
excerpt: As mentioned in my previous blog post, writing has become my passion. It doesn’t matter where I am; I write. Whether I am at work or out shopping, I’m always jotting down ideas for my books. When it…
html:
As mentioned in my previous blog post, writing has become my passion. It doesn’t matter where I am; I write. Whether I am at work or out shopping, I’m always jotting down ideas for my books. When it came time to write Deadly Vows, the second book in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, I knew the most heartbreaking passage would be the letter Rafael writes to Hannah. Because of the strong, close bond they share, that scene could either make the reader’s heart soar or shatter it completely. Deadly Vows is where Hannah is pushed to her limits, both in life and in understanding who she truly is.

After the accident that leaves her battered and in a coma, she loses the ability to recognize what and who is right in front of her. If Hannah shouted at Jonathan or Bree or grew frustrated with them, I didn’t mind writing those moments, but the letter Rafael writes to Hannah was, without question, the most difficult thing to write.

Probably one of the reasons it was difficult to write was that, throughout the whole book, Rafael spends nearly every waking hour trying to ensure Hannah remembers him. There are several moments when Hannah recalls bits and pieces, yet she also sometimes feels the pressure from Rafael, even though his intentions are sincere and he is trying to help rather than control her. When she has had enough, she yells at him, leaving him heartbroken.

As he steps into his apartment, he makes the painful decision that the kindest thing for both of them—especially for her—is to leave her. Rafael then composes a heartbreaking letter. In it, he recalls for Hannah the moments they shared in Paris. Below is an excerpt from the letter Rafael writes to Hannah. Words cannot fully capture how difficult it was to write this section of the book. Much of it came from creative impulse, but I also drew on personal experiences I have lived through. Before, when I once reunited with someone, my greatest fear was that they would not remember me. I cried for a couple of minutes while I was writing the letter from Rafael to Hannah, the words stirring up memories and emotions I hadn't expected.

“Do you remember Paris, Ma Cherie? The way the city lights danced on the Seine at night? I remember taking you to the Champ de Mars, the cool evening air against our faces as we waited. And then the Eiffel tower, erupting in a cascade of twinkling lights. Your gasps of wonder, the way your hand reached for mine- those moments are etched into my soul. I held you close that night, not just physically. But emotionally, wanting to absorb any lingering shadows that might have haunted you. You were so brave Hannah, so resilient, even after facing such darkness three years ago.”
seo_title: The most heartbreaking thing to write was Rafael’s letter

title: Character Profile: Bree
excerpt: Bree… Bree is a mysterious newcomer in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. Introduced as Daniel’s girlfriend, she’s an intense fan who follows and admires Hannah closely, appearing supportive…
html:
Bree…

Bree is a mysterious newcomer in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. Introduced as Daniel’s girlfriend, she’s an intense fan who follows and admires Hannah closely, appearing supportive while keeping parts of her past concealed. She’s present during Hannah’s identity crisis, offering comfort and encouragement even as questions about her motives quietly surface. Later Bree begins receiving ominous riddles from a hooded figure, is violently attacked, and comes dangerously close to being framed for events she may or may not have orchestrated. But who is she, really? Can she be trusted, or is there more to her story than she lets on?

In Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession she takes on the role of Hannah’s maid of honor, a position that places her even closer to the center of the drama. As the killings continue and tension mounts, Hannah grows increasingly suspicious that Bree may not be entirely honest about her connections and intentions. Should Hannah dismiss her unease as paranoia born of stress, or start watching those closest to her with far more scrutiny than before?

Since the start of Deadly Vows, she has remained an enigmatic figure, never fully revealing whether her intentions are sincere or whether she is instead a woman driven by a hidden vendetta. She is similar to Sofia from Deadly College Murders.
seo_title: Character Profile: Bree

title: Character Profile: Det. Smith
excerpt: Detective Smith Straight to the point. No time to play games. Who is he? Smith made his debut in the first mystery series. Convinced that Hannah was guilty of the college murders, Smith was initially…
html:
Detective Smith

Straight to the point. No time to play games. Who is he? Smith made his debut in the first mystery series. Convinced that Hannah was guilty of the college murders, Smith was initially determined to see her receive the death penalty. However, while she sat in custody, he gradually began to doubt his first impressions and started to believe that Hannah had been truthful from the start — that someone else was responsible for the killings. After she ultimately solved the case, Smith offered her a position on his team, but she politely declined, choosing instead to begin a new life in Paris. Smith respected her decision, and he assured her that the offer would remain open whenever she decided she wanted it.

In Deadly Vows he assumes a more prominent role, becoming one of the trio who aids Rafael in uncovering the truth behind Connie’s murder. During the investigation he suffers a painful loss when his partner, Detective Frigon, is killed in front of him, and Smith vows to see justice done for her death. He grows more cordial with Hannah, though he continues to urge her to steer clear of the investigation for her own safety.

In Paris Noir, Smith plays a crucial part in executing Hannah’s risky plan: he assists in having her arrested so she can draw out the people who wish to harm her loved ones. He is heavily involved in efforts to ensure Donovan leaves both Hannah and Rafael alone, committing himself to protect them and see the case through to its resolution.
seo_title: Character Profile: Det. Smith

title: Perilous riddles and visions beyond the ordinary.
excerpt: When I began Deadly College Murders and started to see the plot taking shape, I realized the main character had to stand apart from familiar tropes. She is neither an Anti‑Hero nor a simple victim…
html:
When I began Deadly College Murders and started to see the plot taking shape, I realized the main character had to stand apart from familiar tropes. She is neither an Anti‑Hero nor a simple victim; she is, above all, a survivor. At first she presents as shy and hesitant, frightened to speak up about the harassment by Professor Gonzalez. As the story progresses and she finds herself accused of terrible crimes, I wanted to explore not only the external mystery but the internal one: the strange riddles left at the crime scenes and, more importantly, Hannah’s recurring premonitory dreams. In those dreams she treads a forest path or walks down the college hallways, only to be struck down by a hooded figure while the tolling of a bell fills the air—images that haunt her waking life and push her to uncover the truth.

As the story progresses and Hannah goes to jail, she continues to have these dreams in which the hooded figure is playing cruel mind games with her, testing her resolve and unraveling fragments of her past. Then, after she unexpectedly receives a symbolic jail-free card and regains her freedom, the people Hannah once interacted with begin to repeat a brutal refrain: she was never able to be faithful to anything or anyone, not even to herself. The book examines the importance of paying attention to those persistent nocturnal visions and suggests that Hannah may—or may not—possess a rare, unsettling gift. Although she at first tries to keep the dreams secret, it is Raf who ultimately discovers that his goddaughter is experiencing visions that go beyond the ordinary and into the dangerous. Having cracked the case in Deadly College Murders, Hannah finds that the riddles and nightmares only grow more dangerous in Deadly Vows, while in Paris Noir one of those dreams may, perhaps, come true. The central message I want readers to take away is simple: pay close attention to Hannah’s dreams, for they hold the clues to the identity of the hooded figure.

With the dreams that she has in the third book, will she make it down the aisle? Or will her happy ending not come true?
seo_title: Perilous riddles and visions beyond the ordinary.

title: The Path of oncoming trains… Hannah and Rafael
excerpt: As mentioned in my previous blog post, a central theme in the three-mystery series is Rafael and the close bond he shares with his beloved goddaughter. Having spent many years as a cop, Raf became a…
html:
As mentioned in my previous blog post, a central theme in the three-mystery series is Rafael and the close bond he shares with his beloved goddaughter. Having spent many years as a cop, Raf became a central figure in Hannah’s life when he left active duty to become a criminal justice professor at her college, not wanting to continue risking his life in the dangerous world of law enforcement. In the first book he helps her unravel the mystery behind the college murders and even pushes for her to be placed in witness protection to keep her safe from being killed. While Hannah appreciated his concern, she has always been fiercely independent and refuses to let her godfather put himself in harm’s way to save her.

Three years later, while in Paris, Raf still sees that Hannah is not herself—haunted by recurring dreams of running through the forest and by the memory of the hooded figure from the first book. Part of Rafael desperately wants to protect Hannah, but she continues to keep him at arm’s length and won’t let him fully step in.

After the accident that leaves her beaten, Rafael does his best to ensure Hannah is protected at all times. Even when she doesn’t know who he is, she still feels the weight and frustration of the constant overprotectiveness he presents. While some readers might interpret his behavior as obsessive or possessive, that is not the intent; he is simply trying to keep her safe. The thought of losing her terrifies him, and that fear drives every careful, sometimes heavy-handed, action he takes.

This brings us to the third book. After he almost loses his life, the day of her wedding, Hannah comes to the decision that now it is her turn to be protective of her godfather, but he knows that she will do her best to protect him. There comes a point in the third book, in which Hannah tells Rafael that “You cannot keep pulling me from the path of oncoming trains.”

The meaning behind this quote is that, despite everything he does, he will come to understand that he cannot fully shield her from harm, no matter how fiercely he tries. Even when Hannah becomes frustrated with him, she recognizes that his intentions are sincere and rooted in genuine love and concern.

Readers will ask themselves “What will happen with Rafael and Hannah? Will their close bond change after the events unfold in the third book?” The answers lie in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession
seo_title: The Path of oncoming trains… Hannah and Rafael

title: The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence… in progress
excerpt: After finishing Paris Noir, I am currently working on my fourth book, The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence. What is this book about? After the events of Paris Noir, Detective Hannah Walker has…
html:
After finishing Paris Noir, I am currently working on my fourth book, The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence. What is this book about? After the events of Paris Noir, Detective Hannah Walker has grown into a hardened, no-nonsense investigator who refuses to waste time. Her sense of humor has all but disappeared, and the bond between her and Raf is beginning to crack. Having lived in Paris for the past couple of years, Hannah is pulled back into a new mystery when she receives a call from Smith, who reports a woman found murdered with a riddle left beside her cold, lifeless body.

Once Hannah and Rafael return to the States, the tension between them explodes into a massive argument, and Hannah angrily tells him off. Not long after, Rafael is kidnapped, and Hannah becomes single-minded in her determination to find her godfather. She manages to rescue him, only to discover the depth of the tragedy: Raf has been poisoned. Now the race is on for Hannah to uncover who is responsible for the toxin running through his veins.

Her search introduces her to a prominent doctor named Stu, who claims to know where the antidote may be found—Lucerne, Switzerland. Armed with this lead, Hannah and Rafael embark on a fraught European journey that takes them to the picturesque but ominous streets of Lucerne. There they learn that the murdered woman was Gonzalez’s ex‑wife, and that she had undergone ECT at the infamous Die Klinik den Geist zu Heilen—a clinic whose promise of “healing the mind” may actually mean erasing it.

Refusing to watch her godfather suffer, Hannah makes a desperate and dangerous choice: she poisons herself with the same toxin so she can share Raf’s symptoms and track down the cure from within the same poisoned reality. As the toxin takes hold, Hannah endures vivid hallucinations and haunting dreams—a never‑ending train, a hallway of mirrors, and a surreal tea with an enemy—that blur the line between memory and menace. Driven by the love for her daughter and determination to save both Raf and herself, Hannah races to find the cure before they are both lost to silence in The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence.
seo_title: The Thirteenth Riddle: A Poisoned Silence… in progress

title: Character Profile: Jonathan
excerpt: By now, readers will know who Jonathan is. For those who are new to the series, Jonathan is the enigmatic man Hannah met in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. He plays a significant role in both…
html:
By now, readers will know who Jonathan is. For those who are new to the series, Jonathan is the enigmatic man Hannah met in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. He plays a significant role in both the second and third books. Jonathan is a young private investigator who aided Hannah during her recovery after the brutal attack she suffered in Deadly Vows. In this third installment of the Hannah Walker Mystery Series, Jonathan and Hannah are preparing for their upcoming nuptials in Paris. But after Rafael is attacked and their investigations take them to Las Vegas, Jonathan begins to behave strangely and starts treating Hannah harshly.

Unknown to Hannah, he harbors a dangerous secret—if she were to discover it, it could cost her life, a risk he cannot afford to take. What Jonathan does not realize is that Hannah has been plagued by recurring dreams in which they never make it down the aisle to say “I do.”

Will Jonathan and Hannah survive these new strings of killings and obsessions? Or will one of them meet their demise? The answers lie in Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession.

When creating the character of Jonathan, I wanted him to contrast with Daniel, the man Hannah fell in love with in Deadly College Murders. Daniel had been more of a crush for Hannah, but when she met Jonathan, everything shifted. His temperament and outlook are markedly different from Daniel’s. In Deadly Vows, Hannah recognizes how deeply Daniel wants to be with her, yet she comes to feel as if he has become a darker, almost cruel version of himself. With Jonathan, however, she experiences a sense of safety and steadiness. He is the one who patiently helps her heal and opens her eyes to how unfairly she treated Rafael. Daniel represents darkness in Hannah’s life while Jonathan represents light.
seo_title: Character Profile: Jonathan

title: Paris Noir: Character Profile… Donovan
excerpt: Who is Donovan? Donovan… the shadowy adversary from Rafael’s past who resurfaces intent on revenge. The spark for his return is Rafael’s refusal to join him after discovering Donovan was a corrupt…
html:
Who is Donovan?

Donovan… the shadowy adversary from Rafael’s past who resurfaces intent on revenge. The spark for his return is Rafael’s refusal to join him after discovering Donovan was a corrupt, dirty cop. In crafting Donovan, I aimed for a ruthless, cold, and calculating antagonist whose presence forces the hero to change. An arch-nemesis must alter the protagonist’s life, and in this series that role falls to Rafael.

Rafael is a former police officer who reinvented himself as a criminal justice professor to shape the next generation of law enforcement. He undergoes the most significant character development in the series, confronting his past choices while striving to live honorably. He is fiercely devoted to his goddaughter, as shown in the first two books, and would go to any lengths to protect her.

Donovan is consumed by obsession and driven to obliterate Rafael’s life. He levels chilling threats against Rafael, specifically targeting the one person Rafael loves most—his goddaughter. With a personal vendetta, Donovan knows Rafael’s history, his mistakes, and the vulnerable spot that could bring him down. Donovan will be the nemesis that will change the course of the series moving forward. How will he change the outcome of the series? Only I would know.

His obsession not only focuses on Rafael but also extends to Hannah. Hannah understands that her godfather wants to protect her at all costs, yet Donovan will stop at nothing to drive a wedge between her and the man who watches over her. He is a man who once murdered many people while hiding behind the authority of his role as a law enforcement officer. In temperament and methods he echoes Doug, the disgraced former cop from Deadly College Murders, whose dark past Rafael investigates in Deadly Vows.
seo_title: Paris Noir: Character Profile… Donovan

title: Paris Noir: Where nothing is as it appears, and the lines of obsession blur past the point of delusion.
excerpt: Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession follows Hannah Walker as she stands just days away from marrying the love of her life, Jonathan when tragedy suddenly strikes: her beloved godfather, Rafael, is brutally…
html:
Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession follows Hannah Walker as she stands just days away from marrying the love of her life, Jonathan when tragedy suddenly strikes: her beloved godfather, Rafael, is brutally run down in what appears to be a deliberate attack. Determined to uncover who was behind the wheel, Hannah digs into Rafael’s past and discovers that a dangerous man from his past has returned — consumed by a dark obsession and intent on destroying him. While Hannah is consumed with worry for Rafael’s safety, she fails to see that the threat may be far closer than she imagines; someone within her circle could be pulling the strings behind the murders.

As wedding preparations continue, Hannah begins experiencing recurring premonitory dreams in which she never gets to say “I do,” visions that haunt her waking hours and push her to act. Driven to stop the new string of killings before more lives are lost, she pursues leads and confronts secrets, all the while blind to the possibility that the person she trusts most might be the very one working against her. From making sure Rafael stays safe, to meeting a stunning illusionist on a plane, Hannah will do whatever it takes to say “I do.”

This story was inspired by a visit to the City of Light, Paris — a backdrop that provided the mood and momentum I wanted for my third novel. After finishing Deadly College Murders, written during my own college years, and Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes, which expanded the focus to include Rafael’s close bond with Hannah, I knew this third installment had to center on Rafael’s fierce protectiveness and the lengths he would go to keep his goddaughter safe. Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession reveals how deeply Rafael loves Hannah and how he’s willing to risk everything — even his life — to ensure she remains unharmed.

The story also explores the themes of obsession and revenge, revealing how Sin City and the city of love is far more dangerous and unpredictable than one might initially believe.
seo_title: Paris Noir: Where Nothing Is as It Appears

title: Rafael and Hannah… an unbreakable bond
excerpt: It all started with Deadly College Murders and continues through to Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession. When I began Deadly College Murders, what started as an innocent campus love story deepened into an…
html:
It all started with Deadly College Murders and continues through to Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession. When I began Deadly College Murders, what started as an innocent campus love story deepened into an unbreakable bond between Rafael and Hannah. That profound connection becomes one of the central themes of the Hannah Walker Mystery Series. Hannah, a young college student accused of murders on campus, insists on handling things herself at first. But when her godfather Rafael intervenes, she reluctantly allows him back into her life after years of distance, driven by fear of losing him. Together they uncover the conspiracy behind the college killings, and Rafael takes Hannah to Paris, where their relationship grows even stronger.

After Hannah’s accident she loses memory of the closeness they once shared, and it falls to Rafael to help her remember how deep their bond ran. In Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession their connection surpasses all prior expectations—Hannah is determined to do whatever it takes to keep Rafael by her side, because losing him is her greatest fear. Rafael, meanwhile, keeps painful secrets to try to protect his goddaughter from harm. Hannah repeatedly has to remind him that he cannot keep pulling her from the path of oncoming trains; she loves his devotion, but neither of them can save the other from every threat they face.

What makes it even more beautiful is how deeply Rafael loves his goddaughter. Perhaps one of the most difficult scenes for me to write was the letter Rafael pens to Hannah near the end of Deadly Vows, written before she fully understands who he really is and before the weight of guilt settles on her after reading it. I cried a lot while composing that letter—especially during the part where she yells at him, and when he recalls their shared adventures in Paris. The memories he describes are vivid: the long walks along the Seine, the quiet mornings in small cafés, and the way the Eiffel Tower would sparkle at midnight, casting a fragile, luminous comfort over them. Their bond will strengthen even more in The Thirteenth Riddle: A poisoned silence, where he will once again be front and center.

How much will their special bond shift after the final chapter of Paris Noir? Stay tuned…

When I started writing Deadly College Murders back in 2019, I had no idea how much this project would evolve and grow. Throughout the challenges of the pandemic, I kept immersing myself in mysteries and crime stories, which fueled my writing even more. While working on the first book, I was already inspired to begin the second one, Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes. Upon finishing that, I realized the third installment had to be something truly spectacular—an opportunity to go big or go home. I felt compelled to include more deadly twists, complex riddles, and unexpected turns to captivate readers even further. From the very start, I knew that Hannah’s story would not have a happy ending. For the third book, I chose to center the narrative on the enigmatic figure who would leave audiences questioning—Rafael. He’s Hannah’s protective godfather, a man who transitioned from a career in law enforcement to becoming a college professor. But who is Rafael really? Where did he come from? And how will Donovan, a relentless antagonist, make Rafael’s life an unending nightmare? These are the questions that shape the intense and gripping drama of the final chapter.

Donovan will make Rafael’s life an absolute living hell. From a daring heist at an ancient pyramid, to a terrifying incident where Rafael is nearly run down, to Hannah’s shocking arrest and a chance encounter with a mysterious illusionist, it falls upon Hannah and Rafael to confront the dark demons of their troubled past. Only then can they hope to return to Paris, where Hannah is set to marry the love of her life, Jonathan. But with Hannah plagued by disturbing premonition dreams, will these ominous visions prevent her from ever saying the fateful words “I do?” The answer lies firmly within the thrilling pages of Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession.

title: Meet the characters!

html:
Hannah Walker

The main protagonist of the Hannah Walker Mysteries series, Hannah is a dedicated Criminal Justice major who unexpectedly finds herself drawn deep into a dangerous world filled with deadly riddles, chilling crimes, and strange premonitory dreams. With aspirations to become a brilliant detective like Sherlock Holmes, she quickly learns that sometimes it's better not to wish for something too eagerly—because when you do, you might just get it in the most unsettling way. When her inappropriate professor, Gonzalez, is found murdered on the college campus, Hannah initially wants to avoid any involvement. However, everything changes when a janitor is mysteriously thrown from a roof. As the horrifying deaths continue, with one campus member after another falling victim, all signs disturbingly point back to Hannah. Racing against time and facing growing accusations, she realizes she has no choice but to uncover the truth behind these gruesome murders. With the help of her godfather, Rafael Walker Smith, she must piece together clues and solve the case before it’s too late.

Rafael Walker Smith

The overprotective godfather who loves Hannah more than anything else in this world, Rafael is a deeply devoted and caring figure in her life. A former law enforcement officer, he retired from the force and chose to become a college professor for two main reasons: to protect his goddaughter Hannah and to educate the future generation of police officers. Upon discovering that Hannah was a victim of harassment, he commits himself fully to shielding her from harm, especially when she becomes a prime suspect in the college murders. The strong bond he shares with his goddaughter serves as a central theme throughout the mystery series, highlighting loyalty and unconditional love. Rafael is the steadfast presence who supports Hannah emotionally, holding her hand through the terrifying ordeal of her accusation. In the second book, he takes on an even more pivotal role by helping to uncover the true identity of the killer, all while dealing with the shadows of his own past. Throughout the series, Rafael experiences the most significant character development, evolving from a protective guardian into a complex and determined individual confronting his personal demons. However, there are times when Hannah feels genuinely exhausted by his constant attention, especially whenever he makes an effort to shield her from any perceived danger. She repeatedly reminds Raf that he cannot keep intervening and pulling her away from the path of oncoming trains, no matter how much he insists he’s only trying to protect her.

Sofia

Sofia, once a determined prosecutor who made a significant career shift to become a defense attorney, reenters Hannah's life as an old friend from years ago. She returns just as she receives a pivotal job offer, one that Hannah encourages her to accept, believing it to be the right move. Sofia’s arrival coincides with a critical period when Hannah finds herself in desperate need of support. As Hannah faces accusations of these gruesome murders, Sofia steps in to guide her through the turmoil, pledging unwavering loyalty—but can she truly be trusted? Beneath her compassionate exterior lies a deeper mystery: Sofia is not quite who she claims to be, and dark motives may be driving her actions. Her character grows increasingly complex and morally ambiguous, challenging the audience to decide whether she is a genuine ally or a cleverly disguised antagonist, a suspect or merely a red herring in this unfolding drama. Is she the hidden main villain?

Robert

The man whose wife vanished without a trace over a year ago in Las Vegas. When he arrives in the city, Hannah quickly falls under his captivating romantic spell. However, this man is concealing far more secrets than Hannah could ever begin to imagine. Is he merely a red herring, leading her away from the truth? Or is he perhaps an unexpected ally of one of Hannah’s enemies? Will he be the one responsible for sealing Hannah’s ultimate fate, or could he become the person who comes to her rescue during her most critical trial?

Professor Gonzalez

The professor who is tragically murdered sets the dark and suspenseful tone for the entire plot of the book. Gonzalez was a ruthless and cold-hearted man, showing little to no concern for his students’ well-being. Rafael discovers from Hannah that Gonzalez had been harassing her for some time. Filled with anger, Rafael initially wants to kill Gonzalez, but Hannah warns him that Gonzalez holds considerable power, effectively having the entire faculty under his control and pay. When Gonzalez is ultimately murdered on a dark and stormy night, readers begin to uncover the disturbing secrets he desperately wanted to keep hidden from everyone.

Daniel

Hannah’s best friend, the person she harbors deep feelings for, does not return those emotions. After Hannah is unexpectedly thrown in jail, Daniel takes it upon himself to start his own investigation, determined to be the one who will secure her freedom. What Hannah doesn’t realize is that Daniel actually does have feelings for her, but he struggles to admit them, keeping his emotions carefully hidden. He is often regarded as the Noah Drake figure of General Hospital, known for his charisma and complex personality.

Detective Smith

Smith, the one man who initially believes Hannah is guilty and is determined to throw her in jail. However, as the book progresses, he gradually comes to realize that Hannah is actually a good person who was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time. Over the course of the story, his perception of her changes significantly, and he ultimately becomes her ally in the next two books of the series: Deadly Vows and Paris Noir.

html: I am absolutely thrilled to announce that my third book, Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession, has won an award at the prestigious International Impact Book Awards! I feel both honored and humbled that my third installment in the Hannah Walker Mystery Series has received such acclaim. Through the story of Hannah and her godfather Rafael, readers will be fully immersed from the very moment they open the first book. While I won't reveal how the third installment concludes, I can say that I was genuinely excited about how I crafted the ending—a part of the writing process that I struggled with greatly. When I started writing the second one, I knew it had to be significantly better than the first one, and I realized it was essential to add several unexpected twists and turns to keep readers engaged. The third one focuses entirely on Rafael, exploring his complex past and detailing how his bond with his goddaughter grows deeper and more meaningful over time.

When an unknown figure runs over her godfather Rafael on her wedding day, Hannah is determined to find out who is after her godfather. When she learns from him that a man by the name of Donovan is after him, it is up to Hannah to find out who this man is.

Paris Noir: Deadly Obsession In the city of romance, one obsession turns deadly—and family ties are tested beyond recognition.

Hannah is moments away from saying “I do” to Jonathan in a sunlit chapel tucked in the heart of Paris. But just as the vows begin, a scream pierces the ceremony. Outside, her godfather Rafael—her lifelong protector and emotional anchor—is struck by a speeding car. The crash isn’t just an accident. It’s a warning.

Rafael’s sudden reappearance and near-death experience unravel Hannah’s carefully built future. As she rushes to his side, she’s pulled into a mystery that stretches far beyond the streets of Paris. The accident was no coincidence. Someone wants Rafael silenced—and Hannah implicated.

As riddles begin to surface and cryptic messages appear in places they shouldn’t, Hannah uncovers a web of obsession, betrayal, and psychological manipulation. The deeper she digs, the more she realizes that Rafael’s past—and her own—are tangled in a deadly game that began long before the wedding.

Filled with bloody premonition dreams and deadly riddles, Hannah begins to question everything. Will she make it to the altar and say “I do”? Or will fate—and a killer—strike before her wedding day?

You have to really feel the pain that Hannah goes through in this book, as well as Rafael. I can honestly say that other than Hannah, Raf is the one that suffers the most, because it is personal for him. He has to fight to make sure she is ok. Perhaps one of the most difficult things to me, was writing the letter that Raf writes to Hannah. It broke me so much, that I started crying.

Connie. Connie is the bride that gets murdered before she says “I do.” secrets of who she really was get revealed.

After finding out, who was behind the deadly college murders, Hannah’s life has not been great. She keeps having visions of the person who made her life a living hell. But the one person who is there… Rafael, Hannah’s godfather who has not left her side for 3 years. Although she says, she is fine. She is not. She can not lie to her Godfather. When her best friend Connie calls her, to let her know she is getting married, Hannah flies back to Lake Eden to watch her marriage, unfortunately the unexpected happens: The bride is murdered minutes before she says “I do.” and the worst part? A deadly riddle is left for Hannah at the wedding. Whispers from the past will echo louder and the nightmare begins once again. With the twists through hidden letters, corrupted memories and figures from Hannah’s past, she and Rafael must stay ahead of the killer who is not reliving history, but rather rewriting it. What begins with love… ends with silence in Deadly Vows: Echoes of College Crimes

Hi everyone, my name is Bree and I am the author of Deadly College Murders. The first in the many of the Hannah Walker Mystery Series. How did this book come to fruition? Well, it all started at Cerritos College when I was majoring in Administration of Justice. I went to the library and I was bored out of my mind. As I went into the deep section of the library, I asked myself “Wouldn’t it be interesting if there was a murder in a college and I could be the one to solve it?” I had always had a fascination to solve crimes. Inspired by mystery shows like Forensic Files and the Aurora Teagarden Mysteries, I began writing in the college library. I was constantly going through writer’s block. I found inspiration in my sharp minded professor R.G. His quiet strength and intellect and sharp wit is what would later become a blueprint for Rafael, Hannah’s godfather. As the pandemic surfaced, I continued suffering from writer’s block. However that did not stop me from writing my book. I found myself drawn in watching the Crossword Mysteries Series, Aurora Teagarden Mysteries, Murder she baked series and Picture Perfect Mysteries! The book itself went through some character name changes as well as different titles. One of the original titles was going to be named… Murder at A college. But I settled for Deadly College Murders as it sounded just right. Originally envisioned as a love story between Hannah and Daniel, I settled it for Hannah and the strong bond she has with her godfather Rafael. The pandemic is what inspired me to continue writing my masterpiece and the memories of my former professor R.G is what continued helping me in shaping his character. While the ending was going to end in NYC, I chose to end it in Paris, after living my adventures in Europe!

What is the book about?

Deadly College Murders tells the riveting story of Hannah Walker, a student majoring in Administration of Justice. When her perverted writing professor is found murdered, Hannah wants to investigate, despite warnings of her godfather Rafael. Much like R.G, Rafael is retired from the force and went to teach at a college to be close to his goddaughter Hannah. As the murders in college begin to pile up, Hannah begins to wonder if she is the one that has been committing these murders! Along the way, she meets a dangerous man who she doesn’t know if she can trust him. Her friend Sofia, is a lawyer who moved from NYC to Oregon to be with her, but is she really who she says she is? And then we have Daniel. Hannah’s best friend, whom she is in love with. When she gets accused of the college murders, he helps her investigate. We have Detective Frigon and Smith who are the ones that make Hannah’s life a living hell. As the story moves along, Hannah experiences a lot of premonition dreams and encounters deadly cryptic spine chilling riddles.
seo_title: How Deadly College Murders Came to Be
